410.title: Lanes — who acts
410.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | DTH lead (programme manager) | programme-manager | Owns the handbook. Sets its scope and its place in the DIIG once, forms the technical working group (TWG), and records the roles and RACI that every later lane is scoped against. | . | Work plan (beans) | work-plan | Seeded once from the scope, with one bean per stage and per structured-drafting track, so progress is visible without reading the diagram. | . | Librarian | librarian | Brings every source into the handbook’s library/ as received and frozen: WHO publications through who-iris, TWG outlines and workbooks as uploads. Never edits a source to answer a comment. | . | Business analyst | business-analyst | Drafts the outline and the structured content. Every structured track uses a smart-base DAK block kind and calls the shared edit-and-review subprocess. | . | Terminologist | terminologist | Builds the glossary as a SKOS scheme from the TWG’s candidate definitions and links each term to the smart-ra concept it matches or narrows. Never chooses between conflicting definitions; records them as alternatives. | . | Architect group and handbook owners | reviewer | Review the structured content beside drafting, as QA and not as a gate: the architect group for ArchiMate links and new kinds, the owners of each handbook for content shared with theirs. | . | TWG and contributors | feedback-provider | Comment through the contributor log sheet or on GitHub (a pc: line in any issue or PR conversation). Both channels land in one review store. | . | Editor | editor | Imports comments into the review store, groups them into change sets, decides dispositions, and runs editorial and voice QA. | . | Publication manager | publication-manager | Publishes the final handbook and, when permitted, hands it to the WHO repository. | .

414.title: Editing and HCI validation
414.content: Process_Editing · strict · 17 step(s) . What happens to one proposed change to one content block: drafted, validated mechanically and by review, shown to the editor, and committed to the corpus only if accepted. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

415.content: . | Called by: Content lifecycle, Draft, review and publish | Calls: Close the bean, Open the bean, Evidence for a recommendation, Options analysis | Presented on: no docs page section shows this diagram | Running instances: none recorded | .

416.title: Lanes — who acts
416.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Editor / author (person) | author | Every act the requesting party performs personally rather than through the agent lands here: stating the change, retrieving its evidence, and — once every validation path has reported — ruling on it. The gate sits at Task_ReviewFindings, once the findings exist. | . | Authoring agent (system) | authoring-agent | Produces the proposed change and, once findings exist, weighs the options for it — accept, revise, discard — but stops short of choosing: Call_OptionsAnalysis records that the options were weighed, Task_RecordDecision in the editor’s lane records what was chosen, so one party never both analyses and decides. | . | HCI validation pipeline (system) | validation-pipeline | Forks validation into its four parallel paths and, once every one reports, collates mechanical results and review findings into a single report. It checks nothing itself; it makes sure none of the four is missing before the editor sees anything. | . | Mechanical validation (system) | validation-pipeline | Runs the three checks that need no judgement call — schema and constraints, syntax and link resolution, build and QA gates — in parallel with the non-mechanical review rather than gating on it. | . | Non-mechanical validation (review agent or SME) | reviewer | Supplies the half of validation no checker can perform: whether the change says what the editor meant. Gateway_ReviewerKind escalates from agent review to a human SME specifically when the judgement needed turns clinical or scientific rather than editorial. | .

417.title: Steps
417.content: Every one of the 17 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Describe the intended changeTask_DescribeChange | Editor / author (person) | — | The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet. | . | Open the beanTask_ClaimBean | Authoring agent (system) | calls Open the beanbean-coordination | Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else’s. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached. | . | Gather and verify the evidenceCallActivity_Evidence | Editor / author (person) | calls Evidence for a recommendation | Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate’s authority resolved against its publisher’s own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded.This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations – a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none – and the subprocess’s first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. | . | Draft the block editTask_DraftEdit | Authoring agent (system) | content-authorbefore-after-preview | The authoring agent produces a PROPOSED change. Nothing is written to the corpus yet. For a rendered change it also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) here, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so the preview exists when the parallel review starts. | . | Schema and constraint checksTask_SchemaValidate | Mechanical validation (system) | content-validate | Block schema, label prefixes, required fields, constraint rules. | . | Syntax, spelling and linksTask_SyntaxSpell | Mechanical validation (system) | content-validate | Syntax, spelling, cross-references, citation and link resolution. | . | Build and QA gatesTask_BuildGates | Mechanical validation (system) | content-test | Lean build and proof status, LaTeX compile, FHIR/SUSHI validation, QA axes. | . | Agent review of the changeTask_AgentReview | Non-mechanical validation (review agent or SME) | content-review | A review agent judges what no checker can: accuracy, voice, exposition, whether the change says what the editor meant. | . | Human / SME reviewTask_SmeReview | Non-mechanical validation (review agent or SME) | content-review | Escalated to a human reviewer or subject-matter expert when the change turns on clinical or scientific judgement. A rendered change reaches the reviewer with its before/after preview (skill before-after-preview). | . | Collate findings into a reportTask_CollateFindings | HCI validation pipeline (system) | content-validatecontent-validatecontent-validate | Mechanical results and review findings are merged into one report against the proposed change. | . | Log findings on the beanTask_LogFindings | Authoring agent (system) | todo-manager | Findings are appended to the bean, so the next agent or human sees what is outstanding. | . | Review the findingsTask_ReviewFindings | Editor / author (person) | decision-auditdecision-auditdecision-audit | THE GATE: the editor sees every finding BEFORE anything reaches the corpus. | . | Options analysis accept · revise · discardCall_OptionsAnalysis | Authoring agent (system) | calls Options analysis | On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down.Not between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision: Flow_21b runs Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded.In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.)On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief’s trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. | . | Record the decision and audit noteTask_RecordDecision | Editor / author (person) | decision-audit | A decision is an act ABOUT the findings, not a finding. Record the outcome, every finding it weighed, every finding it overrules — and an audit note saying why it was made, or why a finding in it was left. Each note cites corpus evidence: a witness, another finding, a QA report, a block, a file range. An overruled mechanical finding stays on the record; a gate whose findings vanish when somebody disagrees with them cannot be audited. An agent may assemble the citations and is recorded as proposed_by; the author is whoever decided. | . | Revise the proposed changeTask_ReviseEdit | Authoring agent (system) | content-authorbefore-after-preview | The editor chose revise: rework the proposed change against the findings the editor reviewed, then send it back through validation as a new proposal. The before/after preview is refreshed with it (skill before-after-preview). | . | Commit into the corpusTask_Commit | Authoring agent (system) | corpus-commit-contract | Only now does the change become corpus content, together with its QA sidecars. Subject to the commit-hygiene requirement. | . | Close the beanTask_ResolveBean | Authoring agent (system) | calls Close the beantodo-manager | Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine’s resolve sees nothing left but the archive step. | .

The question is about the change, not about who is available. | no → Agent review of the changeyes → Human / SME review | . | Accept, revise or discard?Gateway_EditorDecision | The editor’s recorded decision, with its audit note. revise reworks the proposed change; discard ends with the change dropped; accept commits it into the corpus. | revise → Revise the proposed changediscard → Close the beanaccept → Commit into the corpus | . | How did it end?GW_BeanClosedHow | Which outcome the bean was closed with, so each ends at its own named end event. The bean is closed once, on every path (bpmn-authoring: open and close the bean at the top, once). | in the corpus → Change is in the corpusdiscarded → Change discarded | . | Bean claimed?GW_BeanYours | Reads which end Process_BeanOpen reached. claimed: the bean is in progress and this process works it. not yours: a sibling session or a human holds it, nothing was written to it, and this process stops here rather than work a bean it does not own (bean-coordination). | claimed → Gather and verify the evidencenot yours → Not yours — left alone | .

420.title: Evidence for a recommendation
420.content: Process_EvidenceRetrieval · strict · 10 step(s) . Frame a question for a recommendation, retrieve and appraise evidence from trusted sources, and either attach it or record the gap; a change that states or alters no recommendation ends at its own event before any search. Evidence comes from three classes (trusted L1 sources, trusted L2/L3 content, data repositories), and each candidate’s authority is verified against the publishing body’s own API. STRAWPERSON: registries, grading system and API bindings are not fixed here. i i i i i i i i i i

421.title: How it connects
421.content: . | Called by: Editing and HCI validation | Calls: none | Presented on: no docs page section shows this diagram | Running instances: none recorded | .

422.title: Lanes — who acts
422.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Author / guideline developer (person) | author | Brackets the machine work rather than doing it: frames the PICO before Lane_Agent fans out across evidence classes, then is the only lane that grades what comes back and decides whether it is sufficient for a recommendation; retrieval and authority-checking are delegated. | . | Evidence agent (system) | evidence-agent | Fans out in parallel across the three evidence classes and joins the candidates. It owns coverage, not judgement: grading is Lane_Author’s call and authority is Lane_Trusted’s. | . | Trusted registries and observatories (external) | external-registry | Task_VerifyAuthority and its gateway sit here rather than with Lane_Agent because the decision is a readout of what the external API returns, not this instance’s call; when that answer is uncertain or absent, a bean is opened rather than a verdict invented. | .

423.title: Steps
423.content: Every one of the 10 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Review the existing guidanceTask_ReviewExisting | Author / guideline developer (person) | content-review | The author reads what the document, DAK or IG ALREADY says on this question, before looking outward. A recommendation that contradicts a sibling recommendation in the same artefact is a defect no external evidence will reveal. | . | Frame the question as PICOTask_FramePico | Author / guideline developer (person) | content-author | Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome. The PICO is what makes the search reproducible and the evidence auditable: without it, ‘we looked for evidence’ is not a claim anyone can check. WHO guideline development states the question this way before any retrieval. | . | Search trusted L1 sourcesTask_L1Sources | Evidence agent (system) | document-intake | Ingested primary literature under library/: the sections/*.md tree and, where a document was scanned, ocr/page-NNN.txt. NOTE the known blind spot — a document OCR’d but never re-run through pdf-structure.py has only a stub in sections/, so a sections-only search misses it. | . | Search trusted L2 and L3 contentTask_L2L3Content | Evidence agent (system) | document-intakedocument-intakedocument-intake | Already-adjudicated guidance: WHO SMART DAKs at L2 and FHIR Implementation Guides at L3. A recommendation adopted in a published DAK is evidence of a different kind from a primary study – it is a prior decision, with its own provenance, and must be cited as that rather than laundered into primary evidence.NOT YET SKILL-BACKED: no skill searches adjudicated L2/L3 content forevidence. corpus-grep is a different task (checking that a gap is reallyopen). | . | Query data repositories and statistical datasetsTask_DataRepos | Evidence agent (system) | document-intakedocument-intakedocument-intake | Indicator and microdata sources. Distinct from the two above because the unit of evidence is a MEASUREMENT with a population, a period and a method, not a claim in prose. | . | Verify authority against the registryTask_VerifyAuthority | Trusted registries and observatories (external) | registry-authority-contract | Each candidate is resolved against the standard API of the body that publishes it, so that ‘authoritative’ is a RESOLVED FACT rather than an assertion in the citation. What is checked: that the identifier resolves at the publisher; that the retrieved record matches what the citation claims; that the version and date are the ones cited; and that the publisher is one this folio has declared trusted. STRAWPERSON: the concrete registry list and endpoints are not settled here – see the cat-harness.processes:policy note. | . | Open a bean for the unverified citationTask_RecordUnverified | Author / guideline developer (person) | todo-manager | An unresolvable citation is not dropped and not silently kept. It becomes a tracked item, so the gap is visible in the work plan rather than surviving as a footnote nobody re-checks. | . | Appraise and grade the body of evidenceTask_AppraiseGrade | Author / guideline developer (person) | evidence-appraisal | Certainty of evidence per the grading system the folio declares. The grade attaches to the BODY of evidence for one PICO question, not to an individual citation – which is why this step is after the join and not inside the fan-out. | . | Record the evidence gapTask_RecordGap | Author / guideline developer (person) | todo-manager | Insufficient evidence is a RESULT. It is recorded as such – an honest gap the guideline can state – rather than being closed by weakening the recommendation until the available evidence supports it. | . | Attach the evidenceTask_AttachEvidence | Author / guideline developer (person) | content-author | The PICO, the graded body of evidence, each verified citation and its resolved authority record are written onto the recommendation block, so a reader can retrace the whole chain from the sentence back to the source. | .

424.title: Decisions
424.content: Every one of the 3 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Does the change state or alter a recommendation?Gateway_RecommendationInPlay | The author answers before any search starts. yes: the change states a recommendation or alters one, and the evidence is gathered as below. no: the change carries none – a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source as a computable graphic adds or changes none – so there is nothing to frame as PICO. The no branch ends at its own event, which records that answer in the instance history; it does not pretend a search was run. The answer is the author’s and the editor still rules on the change at Task_ReviewFindings in Process_Editing, so a wrong no is caught there. | yes → Review the existing guidanceno → No recommendation in this change | . | Authority confirmed?Gateway_Authoritative | Answered by checking the source against the observatory or registry API: is its authority confirmed? no opens a bean for the unverified citation; yes goes on to appraise and grade the evidence. | no → Open a bean for the unverified citationyes → Appraise and grade the body of evidence | . | Sufficient for a recommendation?Gateway_Sufficient | Answered by the appraisal: is the graded evidence enough to support a recommendation? no records the evidence gap; yes attaches the evidence to the recommendation. | no → Record the evidence gapyes → Attach the evidence | .

426.title: Worked Example: IPS Pilgrimage (Hajj)
426.content: . This page is a worked example. It applies the business processes A, B, C, F and I of this guide to one case: the IPS Pilgrimage (Hajj) implementation guide (smart-ips-pilgrimage, FHIR R4, IHE PCF 1.1.0). It follows the analysis written for folio-assistant#2702 on 2026-10-30. The case: during Hajj, the host country (KSA) is the VHL Receiver. It asks the pilgrim’s origin country (for example Malaysia) for the pilgrim’s International Patient Summary (IPS) over a Verifiable Health Link (VHL). The origin country’s health information exchange (HIE) is the VHL Sharer. The IPS carries two consent statements from the pilgrim, and those two Consents are the policy for the exchange. The page does not change the IPS Pilgrimage guide. The gaps below say what that guide, or the specifications it uses, would need. Gap G1 has since been resolved in that guide by smart-ips-pilgrimage#3. The pilgrim’s consents are the policy . For Hajj, there is no separate data sharing agreement for the Sharer to look up. The pilgrim’s two Consents are the policy, and each is coded in Consent.policyRule (owner, Q-DRAIN-5, 2026-11-01 07:44Z). That is how the IPS Pilgrimage guide models them since smart-ips-pilgrimage#3. policyRule holds a code from that guide’s IPS.HAJJ.CONSENT CodeSystem, with coding.version set to the CodeSystem version whose consent text the pilgrim was shown. Any arrangement between KSA and the origin country, such as a memorandum of understanding, stays outside the computable decision. Each Consent binds the party it names: . | Consent | What it allows | Who is bound, and where it is checked | . | Origin release (CONSENT-<origin>, for example CONSENT-MYS) | The origin HIE may release the IPS to the KSA Ministry of Health, as information recipient, for treatment, during the Hajj period. | The origin HIE. It enforces this Consent from its own Consent Registry ([ITI-108]) at step 10. The Consent’s decide() result is one row of the default DMN decision PHW.DT.AgreementAccess (PHW.F.10). | . | Host use (CONSENT-KSA) | The KSA Ministry of Health may use the IPS for care during Hajj and any follow-up. | KSA, which follows it after receipt (step 14). The origin does not enforce it. | . The receiver is identified by trust: its key or certificate is accepted in the ips-pilgrimage trust domain (PHW.I.2, PHW.I.3). There is no agreement lookup at PHW.I.4. “Patient-mediated” then means three things, each an existing mechanism: . | The pilgrim records the consents (PCF [ITI-108], process A). | The pilgrim carries the link (the VHL QR code, [ITI-YY4], process C). | The pilgrim is present at the encounter. Giving the passcode (the VHL P flag; ITI-YY5 §2:3.YY5.5.8) is the in-person act. | . The registry copy is enforced; the IPS copy is evidence. The IPS Bundle also carries copies of both Consents. They travel with the data as evidence for KSA. The Sharer does not enforce them: it enforces the copy in its own Consent Registry. The IPS is signed once, when it is issued, so its copy cannot show a later withdrawal (consent rule 4). The flow, step by step . The Hajj encounter, mapped onto VHL and onto the activities of this guide. Steps that hit a gap name it; the gaps are listed in the next section. Before Hajj . | # | Step | Actor | PHW activities | Transaction | Gap | . | 1 | Trust. The origin HIE publishes its signing keys to the ips-pilgrimage trust domain. GDHCN is the trust anchor here, as one option among others. KSA must also publish its own keys or certificates there, so that the origin can authenticate it at step 9. | Origin HIE, Trust Anchor | PHW.B.1, PHW.B.2 | [ITI-YY1] | G3 | . | 2 | Registration. With the OAuth with SSRAA option, KSA’s EMR registers with the origin HIE by UDAP (HL7 SSRAA), using a certificate that chains to an anchor of the ips-pilgrimage trust domain. With HTTP Message Signatures, nothing is registered: the origin reads KSA’s key from the trust list. No agreement URL is involved. | Origin HIE, KSA EMR | PHW.D.9, PHW.D.10 | — | G3 | . | 3 | Counselling and consent. A counsellor explains the plain-language text of each consent (consent rule 3). The wallet records both Consents in the origin’s Consent Registry. Each Consent’s policyRule names which Hajj consent it is (CONSENT-<origin> or CONSENT-KSA), and its coding.version names the IPS.HAJJ.CONSENT version whose text the pilgrim was shown. That version pins the text, which is the role consent rule 2 gives policy.uri elsewhere. | Pilgrim, Consent Recorder, Consent Registry | PHW.A.1, PHW.A.2, PHW.A.3, PHW.A.5, PHW.A.6 | [ITI-108] |   | . | 4 | IPS. The origin HIE generates the Hajj IPS Bundle, with both Consents as entries, and signs it. | Origin HIE | — (IPS Pilgrimage guide) | — | G2 | . | 5 | VHL. The wallet asks for a VHL with a passcode and an expiry. The Sharer checks that the Consents are active, then signs the link. The link’s expiry should not run past the Consents’ provision.period. | Pilgrim, Origin HIE | PHW.B.3, PHW.B.4, PHW.B.5, PHW.B.6, PHW.B.7 | [ITI-YY3], [ITI-108] |   | . At the encounter in KSA . | # | Step | Actor | PHW activities | Transaction | Gap | . | 6 | The pilgrim shows the QR code and gives the passcode. | Pilgrim | PHW.C.1 | [ITI-YY4] |   | . | 7 | The KSA EMR verifies the HCERT/CWT signature against the trust list. | KSA EMR, Trust Anchor | PHW.C.2, PHW.C.3, PHW.C.4 | [ITI-YY2] |   | . | 8 | The KSA EMR registers the pilgrim with the pilgrimage number. | KSA EMR | — (IPS Pilgrimage guide, step 03) | — |   | . | 9 | The KSA EMR sends Retrieve Manifest with the passcode, authenticated by one VHL option. The IPS Pilgrimage guide uses mTLS node authentication ([ITI-19]) today, which is not one of VHL’s options. | KSA EMR | PHW.I.1 | [ITI-YY5] | G3, G4, G5 | . | 10 | The origin HIE decides. (a) It authenticates KSA by trust in the ips-pilgrimage trust domain. There is no agreement lookup: the Consents are the policy. (b) It searches its own registry for the pilgrim’s active origin-release Consent (policyRule = CONSENT-<origin>). (c) It evaluates that Consent with decide() (see the conditions below). The result is the Consent’s row in the default DMN decision PHW.DT.AgreementAccess, whose outcome routes the request. (d) Anything missing gives unknown, and unknown is never permit. | Origin HIE, Consent Registry | (a) PHW.I.2, PHW.I.3; (b) PHW.I.5 → PHW.F.8, PHW.F.9; (c) PHW.F.10; (d) PHW.F.11, PHW.I.6 or PHW.I.7 | [ITI-YY5], [ITI-YY2], [ITI-108] | G2 | . | 11 | Audit. The origin HIE records an audit event. It cites the governing Consents by policyRule code and CodeSystem version, the id and meta.versionId of each Consent read for the decision, which of them permitted, the DMN decision used, the receiver, the purpose, and the documents released or the refusal. | Origin HIE, writing to the Audit Record Repository | PHW.I.9 (with PHW.G.1) | [ITI-20] |   | . | 12 | The origin HIE returns the List and its DocumentReferences (_include=List:item, VHL’s Include DocumentReference Option), then the IPS. | Origin HIE | PHW.I.6 | [ITI-YY5], [ITI-68] |   | . | 13 | The KSA EMR verifies the IPS signature, stores a copy and shows it. | KSA EMR | PHW.I.11 | — |   | . | 14 | KSA follows CONSENT-KSA after receipt. Its duties (for example, keep the IPS for follow-up care only) come from that Consent’s text. Nothing machine-readable travels with the document to say so yet. | KSA Ministry of Health | process G (PHW.G.5, PHW.G.6) | — | G6 | . When does step 10 permit? Only when every one of these holds: . | the passcode is valid; | the link has not expired; | the origin-release Consent is active in the origin’s own registry; | the KSA Ministry of Health, as verified by trust in the ips-pilgrimage trust domain, is the consented actor (provision.actor); | the purpose is treatment (provision.purpose = TREAT); | today is inside the Hajj period (provision.period). | . The origin-release Consent is found by its policyRule code (CONSENT-<origin>), and its coding.version names the consent text the pilgrim was shown. The KSA-use Consent binds KSA, not the origin, so the origin does not need it to permit. With only one Consent applicable, the default DMN decision returns that Consent’s own result. Gaps . Ordered by how much each one blocks a computable decision. Each row names the existing standard that would close it. Nothing here invents a field. | Gap | What is missing | What would close it | . | G1. The Hajj consents are not computable as written. Resolved by smart-ips-pilgrimage#3. | Was: the consent type sat in provision.purpose, the examples had display names only, and policyRule.text was "some policy", so decide() would return unknown every time. Still open in that guide: the consent texts for two origin countries (CONSENT-IDN, CONSENT-OMN) are placeholders (consent rule 3). | HajjConsent now requires policyRule with an IPS.HAJJ.CONSENT code and coding.version (CodeSystem version 2.1.0). policyRule also satisfies R4 invariant ppc-1, so no policy.uri is needed. It also requires provision.actor (an Organization by identifier, role IRCP), provision.purpose from v3 PurposeOfUse (TREAT), and provision.period. See the examples below. | . | G2. Which copy of a consent counts. | The specifications do not say whether the Sharer enforces the registry copy or the copy inside the IPS, or what KSA should do with its copy. | A rule in the implementation guide, not a new field: the Sharer enforces the registry copy (PCF [ITI-108]); the IPS copy is evidence, carrying its meta.versionId so that KSA can cite it. | . | G3. mTLS is not a VHL option. | The IPS Pilgrimage guide’s sequence diagram still authenticates the KSA node with mTLS ([ITI-19]). Since smart-ips-pilgrimage#3, its transaction page says that mTLS is not one of VHL [ITI-YY5]’s three options and recommends OAuth with SSRAA. How KSA’s certificate or key is published in the ips-pilgrimage trust domain is still not specified. | Choose one VHL option: OAuth with SSRAA (UDAP), approved for process D and I, which is X.509-based like mTLS; or HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421). KSA publishes the matching key in the trust domain ([ITI-YY1]). | . | G4. The facility and the clinician are invisible. | CONSENT-KSA is limited to healthcare facilities in the Hajj district, but the request comes from one national KSA EMR. With HTTP Message Signatures, the Sharer sees only KSA, so it cannot check the district limit and the audit cannot name who looked. | HL7 SSRAA: the hl7-b2b extension carries organization_id and the requesting user (SSRAA §5.2.1.1). | . | G5. The purpose of use is not carried. | [ITI-YY5] has no purpose parameter, so the decision assumes TREAT from the Consent’s provision.purpose. This is open point 3 of process I. | HL7 SSRAA purpose_of_use in hl7-b2b (SSRAA §5.2.1.1), with HL7 v3 PurposeOfUse codes. | . | G6. KSA’s duties after receipt are not machine-readable. | CONSENT-KSA allows “any follow up care” and says nothing about retention or onward sharing. Nothing in VHL, IPS or PCF carries such obligations with the document. | Either HL7 Data Segmentation for Privacy (DS4P) obligation codes in meta.security (needs owner approval: not final), or, with approved standards only, KSA keeps following the CONSENT-KSA text it is bound by and audits against it in process G, with no labels on the document. | . | G7. What the audit event cites. Resolved by smart-ips-pilgrimage#3. | Was: the IPS Pilgrimage guide had [ITI-20] at the origin HIE but did not say what the event contains. | That guide now states it, as process I gives it (PHW.I.9): the Consents by policyRule code and CodeSystem version, each Consent’s id and meta.versionId, receiver, purpose and documents released or the refusal. KSA, as an ATNA Secure Node (VHL Vol 1 §1:XX.3), also audits what it receives. IHE BALP patterns need owner approval. | . | G8. Break the glass has no VHL. | In phase 2 of the IPS Pilgrimage guide (process 5.0) the pilgrim may be unconscious: no QR code and no passcode, so the lookup is by pilgrimage number, outside VHL entirely. | Its own search transaction (likely IHE PDQm [ITI-78] with IHE MHD [ITI-67]), a separate opt-in Consent (the wallet’s “break the glass” setting), and the emergency purpose of use ETREAT. Not specified today. | . | G9. Versions and status. | The IPS Pilgrimage guide does not depend on VHL. It describes the VHL steps in its own transaction pages, partly in older SMART Health Links wording (“modified ITI-67”). Its HajjConsent notes on FHIR R5 (verification.verifiedBy, Consent.period) are for later. | Depend on IHE VHL and cite it as what it is: 1.0.0-comment, a public-comment ballot. The guide’s _include=List:item already matches VHL’s Include DocumentReference Option. FHIR R4 with PCF 1.1.0 already matches the approved PCF version. | . Example consents . The two Consents below match the HajjConsent examples of smart-ips-pilgrimage#3. They are FHIR R4 resources on the IHE PCF 1.1.0 profile IHE.PCF.consentIntermediate, which HajjConsent is built on. This guide is built on FHIR R4 4.0.1 too, and the two are instances of its PHW Explicit Consent profile: each names a Hajj consent code in policyRule and has the consent text the pilgrim was shown as its evidence. Every name, identifier, URL and date is a fictional example: . | The pilgrim, the Malaysian HIE and the Saudi Ministry of Health are stand-ins, as in smart-ips-pilgrimage#3. Their identifiers are example.org URLs. | 2025-05-01 to 2025-08-31 stands in for the Hajj period (Hajj 1446/2025, as the IPS.HAJJ.CONSENT 2.1.0 text says), with time for follow-up care. | . Both Consents permit the same recipient, for the same purpose and period. They differ in which Hajj consent they are (policyRule), and so in the text the pilgrim was shown (sourceAttachment) and in whom they bind: the first lets the origin release the IPS, and the second lets the host use it. Only existing elements are used: policyRule (with coding.version), provision.actor, provision.purpose and provision.period. There is no policy.uri, because there is no separate agreement. The instances are in this guide’s artefacts: PilgrimConsentOriginRelease and PilgrimConsentHostUse, both PHW Explicit Consent, with the pilgrim, the origin HIE and the host Ministry of Health. How step 10 reads them: the origin HIE takes the active Consent whose policyRule is its own release code (CONSENT-MYS) from its registry (PHW.F.8). It matches provision.actor.reference.identifier against the receiver as verified by trust in the ips-pilgrimage trust domain (PHW.I.2), provision.purpose against the purpose (TREAT; see G5), and provision.period against today. That Consent’s decide() result feeds the default DMN decision PHW.DT.AgreementAccess (PHW.F.10). PilgrimConsentHostUse (CONSENT-KSA) binds the host Ministry of Health after receipt and is not part of the origin’s decision. The audit event (PHW.I.9) cites each Consent read, by policyRule code and version and by the id and meta.versionId the registry assigned at PHW.A.5. Open questions for the owner . | G6: approve DS4P obligation codes, or keep KSA’s duties in the CONSENT-KSA text only? | G8: is break the glass in scope now? | . Edit this page on GitHub .

427.doc: Staging a feature branch preview, and taking it down
427.title: Staging a feature branch preview, and taking it down
427.content: Process_FeatureStaging · strict · 12 step(s) . The lifecycle of a feature branch’s review preview: staged on a push, taken down when its pull request closes, or removed by an explicit dispatch. THE LIFECYCLE OF A REVIEW PREVIEW, drawn rather than described. Bean 7yvd, owner: “make sure all workflows documented as bpmn”. This is the first .github/workflows/*.yml documented here, and it was chosen because its shape was the least visible: three jobs, eight if: branches, a confirmation gate and a deletion trigger, written down only in a sixty-line YAML comment. Three entry points, and they are three different processes sharing a file. A pull request opened or pushed to STAGES a preview. A pull request CLOSED asks whether the preview should go. A dispatch removes ONE preview that the first two can no longer reach — bean w2g5: the health sweep can only ever report a preview whose pull request is already closed, so by the time anybody reads the finding the event has fired, the job has run and the label was absent. Labelling afterwards fires nothing. TWO GATEWAYS, and both are three-state rather than yes/no. Removal confirmed? reads a merge as confirmation in its own right (bean 1feu) while still requiring a label for a close without a merge. Still in use? refuses on a live signal AND on could-not-tell, because a preflight that has gone blind must not read as permission. EVERY PATH THAT CHANGES branches/ WRITES TO THE RENDER LOG, and the two removal paths write the record in the SAME COMMIT as the removal. A separate log push can fail alone and leave a preview that vanished with nothing saying why, which is the state bean plj1 left the publish branch in for months. The single human step is the dispatch confirmation. Everything else is mechanical, which is what makes build-pipeline the right lane rather than a convenient one. i i i i i i i i i i i i

429.doc: Staging a feature branch preview, and taking it down
429.title: Lanes — who acts
429.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | CI/CD Pipeline | build-pipeline | Runs all three entry points — stage, cleanup, cleanup-dispatch — as one actor because none of the work in any of them needs judgement; the one step that does, confirming a dispatch deletion, was carved out into Lane_Human rather than left here. Every path that changes branches/ writes its render-log entry in the SAME commit as the change, because a log push that can fail on its own is exactly how a preview vanishes with nothing on the branch saying why.A FOURTH trigger starts none of them, and that is deliberate rather than an omission from this diagram. merge_group is declared on the workflow so it REPORTS in the merge queue — a required check that never reports on a merge_group event leaves every queued pull request pending forever — and all three jobs skip on it. A preview exists for the reviewers of a pull request; a queue entry has none and lives for minutes. Without the skip, stage’s existing guards all pass on a queue run (github.event.action is empty and the event is not a dispatch), so it would publish branches/<slug>/ named after the ephemeral gh-readonly-queue/... ref, and nothing would ever remove it — Start_Closed below fires on pull_request_target: closed, and a queue branch is never a pull request that closes. That is the plj1 shape arriving once per MERGE rather than once per pull request. | . | Human actor | user | The only lane whose actor cannot be a machine — deletion-requires-confirmation is not satisfied by a click, so H_Confirm must repeat the slug rather than approve generically, which is what stops a confirmation from an earlier run being replayed against a different preview. It precedes Start_Dispatch rather than following it, so the dispatch entry point cannot fire at all until this lane has acted. | .

430.content: Every one of the 12 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Build the docs siteTask_Build | CI/CD Pipeline | feature-staging | Build the preview from the PR’s head: regenerate the generated docs, trim what this preview does not need, render the BPMN diagrams, then Jekyll, TypeDoc and the knowledge-graph export, with the staging banner and SEO identity claims stripped. It is a PREVIEW build (CAT_BUILD_TYPE=preview, owner 2026-11-01): only what the change reaches, and every whole-corpus index (builtAtPublish entries marked index: true, and the search index) is main’s copy, put back rather than rebuilt. A branch frozen for public comment is dispatched with build_type: full instead. Skill feature-staging, section Build types. A PREVIEW REBUILDS ONLY ITS DEPENDENCY CONE (owner cards Q-CONE-1 C and Q-CONE-2 B, 2026-11-01): main’s writer records say what each derive:publish writer and each step of the QA working copy READ. A writer or QA step whose recorded reads all match is not run, and main’s outputs for it are put back. Every other one runs. QA is not left out of a preview, only narrowed to what the change can reach. Inside a preview’s QA build, skill:register also leaves to derive:publish the two pages that derive:publish builds anyway and that no later QA step reads (skills:docs and lsi:viz), so they are built once. | . | Push to the CDN under branches/Task_Deploy | CI/CD Pipeline | calls Render a Knowledge Graph to a CDNrender-kg-to-cdn | A PREVIEW IS THE GENERAL STEP WITH A DIFFERENT ROOT (owner, 2026-09-30: “independent of staging vs publication … just rendering”). Process_RenderKgToCdn, entered with the tree Task_Build rendered, branches/<slug>/ under the site root as the publication root URL, and GitHub Pages as the target, so its gh-pages Tool pushes. For this target the push is keep_files: true with a destination_dir, so it adds one directory beside whatever else is on the branch; it is also RETRIED once: five other workflows push to gh-pages without joining this one’s concurrency group, and a queue does not help because GitHub CANCELS a pending job when a newer one arrives for the same group rather than queueing it. Measured 2026-09-19: three staging runs from three different branches inside 17 seconds, two cancelled. The call returns the push’s status and message; the render log and the PR comment that follow are this process’s own. THE PREVIEW CAP rides in the same commit (owner ruling 2026-10-02, issue #1868: “cap the maximum number of previews (<= 10) and rotate old ones off”, amended 2026-10-04 to a SIZE budget: “Cap by size, not count”, “3gb”): staging-rotate.ts keeps this preview plus the most recently updated others while their total fits MAX_PREVIEW_BYTES = 3 GB and removes the rest, oldest first, each with a removed render-log entry and its record retired into branches/_retired/. Every push attempt re-reads gh-pages and re-decides rather than rebasing, so a lost race never pushes a stale removal. A rotated-off preview is regenerated by the next push to its PR branch. | . | Append rendered to the render logTask_LogRendered | CI/CD Pipeline | render-logging | Its OWN commit, not part of the deploy. The publish action writes only into destination_dir, so an entry riding in _site would land at branches/<slug>/_render-log/ — inside the directory a cleanup removes, which is the one place a record of the removal must not be. continue-on-error: a preview that deployed and whose entry did not is a gap in the record, not a failed deploy. | . | Comment the preview URL on the PRTask_Comment | CI/CD Pipeline | staging-review | Post, or update in place, one comment on the PR giving the preview URL (branches/<slug>/) and the commit it was built from. Pull-request events only. | . | Derive the slug from the head refTask_Slug | CI/CD Pipeline | feature-staging | Derive the slug from the PR’s head ref: every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-] becomes ‘-‘, runs of ‘-‘ collapse, and leading or trailing ‘-‘ is trimmed. It must be one safe path segment, checked by value. | . | Remove the preview and log itTask_Remove | CI/CD Pipeline | deletion-requires-confirmation | ONE COMMIT for the removal and its record. A separate log push can fail on its own and leave a preview that vanished with nothing saying why — which is the exact state bean plj1 left the branch in. render-log.ts refuses a removed entry with no reason, so this step fails loudly rather than writing a record that says an artefact went and not why. | . | Append retained, with why it staysTask_LogRetained | CI/CD Pipeline | shared step GT_LogRetainedrender-logging | Records that a removal was considered and refused, or that a preview still stands because a signal fired; without the entry that leaves no trace, and nobody can tell why a preview is still up. A reason is REQUIRED — the tool refuses without one. | . | Post the retention notice on the PRTask_Notice | CI/CD Pipeline | staging-review | Removal was not confirmed, so the preview stays: post a retention notice on the PR giving its URL and saying it has NOT been removed, and the two ways to remove it: the staging:cleanup label while the PR is open, or, once it is closed, a Run workflow dispatch with cleanup_slug and a matching cleanup_confirm. | . | Check the slug and its confirmationTask_Validate | CI/CD Pipeline | deletion-requires-confirmation | Guarded three ways because a dispatch input is a DELETION TRIGGER. workflow_dispatch is available only to an actor with write access; the slug must match exactly the characters the sed pipeline can produce, with . and .. refused by name; and the confirmation must repeat the slug, so a confirmation cannot be carried over from an earlier run against a different preview. | . | Re-evaluate liveness AT REMOVAL TIMETask_Preflight | CI/CD Pipeline | deletion-requires-confirmation | Re-evaluated AT REMOVAL TIME, through the same previewLiveness the health sweep uses rather than a second implementation of it. The sweep runs daily and proposes; this acts. Between them a branch can come back to life — bean w2g5 documents exactly that, a session reusing one branch across five successive pull requests. | . | Remove it AND append removed — one commitTask_RemoveDisp | CI/CD Pipeline | deletion-requires-confirmation | Say what is going — size and file count — then remove branches/<slug>/ and append removed to the render log in the SAME commit, so a preview cannot vanish without a record of who dispatched it and why. The slug is a dispatch input, so the tool re-checks it by value rather than trusting the guard. | . | Repeat the slug, exactly, to confirmH_Confirm | Human actor | deletion-requires-confirmation | The one step in this process that is a person’s. Repeating the slug is not ceremony: it names the artefact being confirmed, so a confirmation cannot be inherited by a later run pointed at a different preview. | .

452.title: A sub-graph wants to leave
452.content: Process_GraphDetanglement · strict · 8 step(s) . Part of a repository wants to leave, for size or a semantic reason: four gated stages measure it out of the graph before anything moves, and an administrator authorises the extraction. THE FOUR STAGES ARE GATES, NOT ADVICE: nothing moves until the stage before it measures zero, and they are drawn because a rule in prose is one an agent under pressure talks itself past. Each gate here is a DECISION TABLE: workflow_complete refuses a hand-supplied outcome at a cat-harness.processes:decision gateway, so the branch is computed from the counts a tool already produced rather than asserted. THE SHARPEST GATE IS Detangled?, AND IT IS SHARP BECAUSE OF ITS RULE ORDER. unassignedEdges &gt; 0 returns unknown BEFORE the cross-edge rule is reached, so a zero cross-edge count over an unjudged corpus cannot be read as a pass: unassigned edges are edges the tool declined to judge, not clean ones. A person can skip that rule; a table cannot. EVERY GATE HAS A THIRD STATE AND NONE OF THEM RENDERS IT AS CLEAN. Declared in place? answers unknown on a declaration that did not parse rather than “not yet”, because one says the work has not started and the other says nobody can tell. Detangled? answers unknown on an incomplete measurement. Both route to End_Unknown, which is a REFUSAL to advance — the process stops rather than proceeding on a guess. DECLARING IS CHEAP AND EXTRACTING IS EXPENSIVE, WHICH IS THE POINT. Stage 1 moves nothing: the sub-graph is declared where it already sits, still inside the repository, still connected. STAGE 2 IS A LOOP, AND THE LOOP IS LOAD-BEARING. Prune, merge, factor, or reclassify returns to Measure rather than to the gate, because an assignment is verified by RE-RUNNING and never by being locally reasonable. The four moves are the only four: the first three are the block-scale rule, and “the classification is wrong” is the fourth the repository scale adds because a module’s layer is in doubt the way a block’s chapter is not. ISOLATION IS NOT ZERO EDGES. A sub-graph with no inbound edges can still carry no declaration, no namespace and no published artefact, and lifting that directory produces a repository that cannot say what it is. bootstrap/ is the demonstrated case and the shape to match. THE EXTRACTION IS A PERSON’S DECISION, AND THE LANE SAYS SO. Authorise the extraction sits in the Administrator lane because an extraction moves durable artefacts out of a repository, and deletion-requires-confirmation is not a courtesy the agent may waive: the agent reports what would move, and waits. The administrator lane is the one whose activities change the substrate every other diagram’s lanes bind to, which is exactly what a repository cut does. i i i i i i i i

458.title: Guideline Updates
458.content: Process_GuidelineUpdates · strict · 8 step(s) . Taking up a new version of a guideline, or a changed lower layer, is a re-pin and a review at once. The steward maps the affected layers and re-pins them in dependency order. For each re-pin, the adaptation team compares the old version, the new version and its own adaptations. A change that touches no adaptation or policy merges on the technical path. One that does goes to the adaptation committee, which decides for each adaptation whether to keep, revise or retire it. Revisions are ordinary content changes (Process_ContentChangeReview), and the re-pin merges with them. The loop runs until every layer is current. i i i i i i i i

470.title: A harness’s default rendering
470.content: Process_HarnessRendering · strict · 7 step(s) . Renders a harness instance as its default interface: its left-hand nav and docs on its own theme’s art, and a board of its todos and beans from which a reader reads, reviews and, when a write tool is available, proposes changes into the publication review. The theme art goes behind every docs page. Read-only is the floor. Whether the reader may write is a question about the tools the session has (git-push, github-api, github-connector) and the reader’s permissions, so the gateway reads capabilities and never assumes one write path. A change a reader proposes enters the content change review in folio-assistant-core (content-change-review.bpmn); this process enables that review and does not replace it. i i i i i i i

476.title: Human–agent discussion
476.content: Process_HumanAgentDiscussion · strict (defaulted) · 13 step(s) . A REUSABLE SUB-PROCESS, never an entry point. Every diagram in bootstrap that needs something only a person can supply — a choice, a judgement, a step only they have the rights to perform — reaches it through a call activity with calledElement=”Process_HumanAgentDiscussion”, rather than drawing its own asking. One way of asking, drawn once: a caller that draws its own has a second answer to “how do I ask”, free to drift from this one. BEFORE ANY QUESTION, THE ASKER DETERMINES WHERE IT IS: the CONTEXT, the ROLES, and the PROCESS and TASK (or that it is idle). Each is a task, declared below as a precondition of the first question. WHAT CANNOT BE DETERMINED IS ASKED FIRST, with no default; the caller’s question waits, counted. THE ORDER IS THE PROCESS: context, then options, then a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then one question. A question the reader cannot answer without opening anything is not ready. A DEFAULT is applied only when the CALLER allows one, and is recorded as assumed, never as the person’s answer. Otherwise silence ends as unsettled. SYMMETRIC IN ITS PARTICIPANTS. The answering lane is a person or a sibling agent that already holds the answer; the record says which, because the two are evidence of different weight. NO work-plan element, and isExecutable is false, for the reasons initialize-harness gives. i i i i i i i i i i i i i

Answering, declining and saying nothing are all legitimate moves here, and each has its own end. | .

479.title: Steps
479.content: Every one of the 13 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Determine the context: what is known, and already decidedA_DetermineContext | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the instance’s <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person’s attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. | . | Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person’sA_DetermineRoles | Agent | human-agent-discussion | An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. | . | Determine the process and task, or that you are idleA_DetermineProcess | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: “Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent”. A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one’s rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the Process, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. | . | Ask first about what could not be determinedA_AskUndeterminedFirst | Agent | human-agent-discussion | The caller’s question waits, and is counted (“one more question after this”). What is put first is the undetermined one: the context you could not establish, the Role you are not sure you hold, or the Process you cannot place this in. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. With more than one undetermined, ask about the outermost first (the Process before the Role before the context), since the outer answer usually settles the inner. | . | Say what is being decided, and why it matters nowA_GiveContext | Agent | human-agent-discussion | First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. A link is where somebody goes for more; it is never where the terms are defined. | . | Lay out the options, with what each costsA_LayOutOptions | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Every option the agent could narrow the question to, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. Narrow from context first: an option the agent could have ruled out itself wastes the reader’s attention. | . | Recommend one, and say what happens with no answerA_Recommend | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Mark the option the agent would take and say why. Then say what happens if nobody answers: the default, when the caller allows one, or that the question stays open and the work stops, when it does not. Said now, so silence has a meaning both sides agreed to before it happened. | . | Ask ONE questionA_PutQuestion | Agent | human-agent-discussion | One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Uses whatever channel the caller is in — in bootstrap, the conversation the person is already in. | . | Answer, decline, or say nothingA_Answer | Requestor | — | The Requestor’s move. Declining is an answer. Saying nothing is not, and is what the recommendation’s “if there is no answer” was for. | . | Follow up, narrowerA_FollowUp | Agent | human-agent-discussion | The answer did not settle it: it named a kind rather than an option, or chose two. Ask once more, narrower, naming what the first answer left open. Once: an agent that keeps asking has stopped narrowing. | . | Record the answer, and who gave itA_RecordAnswer | Agent | human-agent-discussion | In the form the caller asked for — for bootstrap’s harness question, a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json with determinedBy asked. Who answered (a person or an agent) is part of the record. An answer about the context, the Role or the Process is recorded the same way, as the person’s word. | . | Apply the stated default, and say soA_ApplyDefault | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Only the default stated in A_Recommend, only where the caller allows one, and recorded as assumed with the default named — never as the person’s answer. The next message to the person says it was applied, so they can reverse it. | . | Record what is still openA_RecordUnsettled | Agent | human-agent-discussion | Declined, or silent where no default is allowed. The record says what was asked and what is still open, so the next actor resumes rather than restarts. Never a guess. When it is the context, the Role or the Process that is still open, say so and stop: a step completed in the wrong Process records an authority that was never given. | .

482.title: Human Translation Workflow
482.content: Process_HumanTranslation · advisory · 16 step(s) . The human half of translation: a coordinator assigns a locale to a qualified translator, the translator works in their own tool, a subject-matter expert judges accuracy, and only then is the result official. You are in this process when a person is doing the translating. translation-workflow is the machine half — extraction, injection, staleness — and it hands off to this one at exactly the point a judgement is needed. The two are separate because completeness is mechanical and accuracy is not: the coordinator’s gate asks whether enough strings are filled, the reviewer’s asks whether they are right, and no amount of the first substitutes for the second. What makes a translation OFFICIAL is the reviewer’s sign-off, never the file being complete. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

The same lane writes the final status.json once sign-off lands, so the official record sits beside the checks that fed it. | .

485.content: Every one of the 16 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Identify content and target localeTask_IdentifyContent | Translation Coordinator | translation-manager | The coordinator selects:- Which content nodes need translation (block, section, chapter, or folio)- The target locale (one of the supportedLocales in <name>.config.json)- The priority and deadline | . | Assign to qualified human translatorTask_AssignTranslator | Translation Coordinator | translation-manager | The coordinator assigns the translation to a qualifiedtranslator, ideally a domain SME for the content area. For WHO content,the translator should be familiar with WHO SMART Guidelines terminology.The assignment includes:- The .pot file(s) from extraction- The domain glossary- Context notes (block kind, chapter, content area)- The deadline | . | Check translation completenessTask_CheckCompleteness | Translation Coordinator | translation-manager | Verify that all msgid entries have msgstr translations.Partial translations are acceptable for initial submissions but must beflagged for follow-up. The coordinator checks:- % of strings translated- Any fuzzy-flagged entries- Missing critical sections | . | Request completion of remaining stringsTask_RequestMoreWork | Translation Coordinator | translation-manager | Return to the translator with a list of untranslatedor fuzzy strings that need attention. | . | Receive assignment and materialsTask_ReceiveAssignment | Human Translator | translation-managertranslation-managertranslation-manager | The translator receives:- .pot file with source strings (msgid)- Domain glossary with approved term translations- Context notes per string- Style guide and WHO terminology referencesTools: Poedit, Weblate, Crowdin, or direct .po editing. | . | Translate strings in preferred toolTask_TranslateInTool | Human Translator | translation-manager | The translator works through each msgid, producingmsgstr translations. They:- Follow the domain glossary for technical terms- Preserve placeholder tokens ({1}, {2}) in position- Mark uncertain translations as #fuzzy- Note any source ambiguities for the coordinator | . | Submit completed .po fileTask_SubmitPO | Human Translator | translation-managertranslation-managertranslation-manager | The translator submits the completed .po file backto the pipeline. This may happen via:- Git commit + push- Weblate/Crowdin sync- File upload to the coordinator | . | Review translation for accuracyTask_SMEReview | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | translation-managertranslation-managertranslation-manager | A subject-matter expert reviews the injected translatedmarkdown for:- Clinical/technical accuracy of terminology- Preservation of meaning from the source- Cultural appropriateness for the target locale- Consistency with the domain glossaryFor WHO content: the SME verifies that normative statements(“SHALL”, “SHOULD”, “MAY”) are translated with the correctforce in the target language. | . | Return for correction with annotationsTask_ReturnForCorrection | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | translation-manager | The reviewer annotates specific passages that needcorrection and returns to the translator with detailed feedback.Each annotation includes:- The passage in question- What is wrong (terminology, meaning, style)- The suggested correction or reference | . | Sign off translation as officialTask_Signoff | Subject-Matter Expert / Reviewer | translation-manager | The reviewer signs off the translation, making itofficial. This records:- signedOffBy: the reviewer’s identity- signedOffAt: the current timestamp- sourceHash: SHA-256 of the source .md- level: block | section | chapter | folioTool: translation_signoff MCP tool | . | Extract the POTTask_ExtractPOT | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_ExtractPottranslation-manager | Scan the source content and write the translatable strings to .pot files at the configured granularity: segment prose by paragraph, shield what must not be translated (math, code, labels, Lean companions) as placeholders, normalise whitespace, and extract metadata such as titles, alt text and captions. Tool: the translation_extract MCP tool. | . | Prepare domain glossaryTask_PrepareGlossary | Automated Pipeline | translation-manager | Builds the locale term base for the target locale from the layered glossaries, has it reviewed, and hands it to the translator with the POT. Each layer’s glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme’s subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term’s translation; an instance layer only adds, and may not give a fixed term a second translation. A match in another subject area is a sense check for the reviewer, not a violation. Previous translations of related content are evidence for a term with no fixed form, not a source that overrides one. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme’s catalogue (translation-manager, “The locale term base”). | . | Inject the POTask_InjectPO | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_InjectPotranslation-manager | Read the .po file and the source .md, substitute msgstr for msgid, unshield the placeholders, and write the translated .md to translations/<locale>/. Check structure (paragraph count, heading levels) and completeness (no empty msgstr), and lint (doubled punctuation, orphaned placeholders). Tool: the translation_inject MCP tool. | . | Round-trip translation QATask_RoundTripQA | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_RoundTripQatranslation-manager | Back-translate the target-language .md into the source language and compare the meaning with the original. It catches semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see, and tells the two apart. Tool: the translation_validate MCP tool.No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, “route drift to a human reviewer”), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. The findings include translation:glossary:check’s: every glossary term translated against the locale term base, fixed before sign-off, with its glossary section in the KG QA report. | . | Append WHO disclaimer (if DAK)Task_AppendDisclaimer | Automated Pipeline | translation-manager | For WHO SMART Guidelines content, automatically appendsthe WHO legal disclaimer:- Translation not created by WHO- English edition is authoritative original- WHO not responsible for translation accuracyOnly applies when folio contentType includes WHO/DAK content. | . | Write status.json (official)Task_WriteStatus | Automated Pipeline | shared step GT_WriteTranslationStatus (official = true)translation-manager | Record the translation’s standing in translations/<locale>/status.json. The official input says which: false records it as unofficial ({ official: false, generatedBy, generatedAt }), usable but shown with a warning badge; true records the human sign-off with the SHA-256 of the source .md, so a later change to the source marks it stale. | .

488.doc: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
488.title: An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
488.content: Process_IgAstCache · advisory · 5 step(s) . How an IG repository’s own site is published, and how the AST it is built from is kept current (skill ig-build-pipeline §”The AST cache lifecycle”). THE RULE. An IG site is built from the IG Publisher AST read from the IG repository’s cache branch cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>, never from Publisher HTML. The publish refuses an AST that is not valid for the commit it publishes (ig-cache.sh restore then verify). A later commit that changes no IG input (sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini, input/) does not make the AST stale. THE REFRESH. The cache is written by ONE thing: fhir-harness’s reusable workflow .github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml, which an IG repository’s Site publish calls as its first job (ast; template templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml). It runs the Publisher through the AST exporter on a GitHub runner (Java, 10 GB heap, tx.fhir.org). It seeds the branch only from a commit on the default branch whose inputs equal the tip’s. A valid AST is a cache, not a release: every page drawn from it carries the provisional mark (ig-ast-delta). i i i i i

491.title: Steps
491.content: Every one of the 5 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Restore and judge the cached ASTTask_Restore | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-ast-deltaig-build-pipeline | ig-cache.sh restore --ig-root . fetches cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id> into output-ast/ (with the Publisher’s txcache/), then ig-cache.sh verify runs ig-ast.ts validity: exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (naming which input), 2 cannot-tell. A restore that finds no branch is a miss, judged as not valid. In an IG repository’s site route this is the first pre step, ig-site:ast (ig-repo-site.ts ast). | . | Build and publish the site from the ASTTask_BuildSite | Site build (agent, stage-local) | ig-render-jekyllig-build-pipeline | Runs the site route’s steps via stage-local.ts → build-instance-site.ts: ig-site:sidecars (IG API sidecars, if the landing layer has the step), ig-site:compose (artefact index and thin pages from the AST, the IG composed at the root), ig-site:openapi (if the IG holds OpenAPI pages), ig-site:publisher-pages (the AST’s resources as ast-data/, the build stamp), and last ig-site:bar (the IG’s slim bar on pages written after publisher-pages). Published at the root from the default branch, as a preview otherwise. | . | Dispatch AST refreshTask_Dispatch | Publication manager (owner, or the agent the owner delegates to) | ig-build-pipeline | Actions → “IG AST refresh (by hand)” → Run workflow on the default branch, inputs ref = the default branch, force = false. Set force = true only to rebuild a cache that is valid but suspected wrong. | . | Build the IG with the AST exporterTask_Export | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | ig-publisher-fork | The runner mounts the layers the IG repository’s index.lock.json pins, then restores and judges the cache itself. When it is not valid (or force is set) it rebuilds with the Publisher fork (Tool ig-ast-export, litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher at the pinned claude/ast-export commit). A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller’s optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit’s input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The AST just built must itself be valid for the commit, or the run fails. | . | Seed the cache branchTask_Seed | AST refresh (GitHub runner: IG Publisher with the AST exporter) | compiled-artefact-cache | ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push: one commit holding the AST, the Publisher’s expansions and txcache/, its subject recording the package, counts, Publisher version and source commit. 494.doc: Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced?
494.title: Is the incremental IG AST what a full build would have produced?
494.content: Process_IgAstDeltaReview · advisory · 4 step(s) . The review step of an incremental FHIR IG build, as its own subprocess: list and inspect the differences between the incremental IG AST and what a full build would have produced, then accept them or raise a finding. WHERE IT SITS. In ig-incremental-build.bpmn it belongs between Task_Merge and Task_Qa: after the restored and rebuilt records are merged, before the QC gates read the aggregate. That diagram does not call it yet; ig-ast-delta §”Where this sits in a process” states the placement. WHAT IT GUARDS. An incremental build rebuilds only the cone of a change, computed on the BASE edges. If the cone rules miss a coupling, a resource that should have changed does not, and nothing downstream can tell: the merged AST looks exactly like a correct one. So a person reads the delta, and a difference nobody can explain is treated as a missed coupling. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM. A clean review says the delta is explained, not that the IG is correct. The AST stays a cache: every rendered page carries the provisional mark, and a release is still cut from a full build (ig-publisher-reduction P4). i i i i

500.content: Process_IgDocsSiteCompose · advisory · 4 step(s) . How a host docs site builds every IG it mounts INSIDE itself, so each IG’s pages wear the host’s chrome (one sidebar, one search, one language selector) rather than being a site of their own. Subprocess of Tool stage-ig-sites; reached from docs-site-publish’s Call_InstanceSites (skill docs-generation). NO IG PUBLISHER RUNS. build-ig-site turns the IG’s source into Jekyll source, with the Publisher’s site.data.fhir filled from the IG’s AST and sushi-config.yaml, and the host’s ONE Jekyll build renders it with just-the-docs (skill ig-render-jekyll). Which IGs is DATA: each instance whose fhir-artifact-index/menu.json records a source.of (the IG repository) and source.ref (the commit). No workflow and no step here names an IG. feature-staging.yml runs the same steps for a pull request’s preview, with --changed-files, so only the IGs a change reaches are rebuilt. An IG repository building its OWN site runs stage-ig-sites --only <instance> --source <checkout> --compose-into <shell> --compose-at-root, which is ig-ast-cache’s Task_BuildSite, not this process. i i i i

505.title: Incremental IG build
505.content: Process_IgIncremental · advisory · 19 step(s) . An incremental build for a FHIR Implementation Guide: compile, validate and re-render only the dependency cone of a change, then gate on QA and deploy. One change (a PR push or a push to main) runs: restore the derived state, compute the change’s dependency cone, compile and validate only the cone against the warm validator, re-render the cone’s records, rebuild the meta-index, assemble the site, gate on QA, then deploy; on main or a release only, seed the cache from the green build. An unusable cache falls back to a full build; an environment error stops the run and logs why. Advisory, like the other content-type pipelines: the package that owns the content owns what adequate means. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

506.title: How it connects
506.content: . | Called by: no call activity names this process | Calls: none | Presented on: no docs page section shows this diagram | Running instances: none recorded | .

507.title: Lanes — who acts
507.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | fhir-modeller | Starts the run with a source change, and owns every failure branch before the process ends rather than just stopping: Gateway_Valid’s no, Gateway_QcPass’s no and Gateway_Restore’s environment error each write to the work plan here, in Task_LogFindings, Task_QcBeans and Task_LogEnvError, before EndEvent_Findings, EndEvent_FindingsQc or EndEvent_EnvError. A run that stops short always leaves a record of why. The work plan is a data store these tasks write to, not a lane of its own. | . | Incremental build (system) | build-pipeline | Owns everything that stays inside the cone: restore the cache, compute the cone, check it out, compile and re-render only that slice, then merge and rebuild the aggregates — Task_Index never re-derives an artefact on its own, so a missing record is a miss rather than a silent rebuild. What needs the JVM’s warm state, it hands to Lane_Services rather than running itself. | . | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publisher-service | Two duties. Task_FullBuild is the fallback when Gateway_Restore finds the cache unusable: it bypasses the cone machinery and reaches Task_Qa on its own. Task_ContextLoad and Task_Validate hold the loaded dependency packages and expansions warm across runs, which makes validating a handful of cone files cheap; losing that warm state is a cache miss and routes to the fallback. | . | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | qc-reviewer | Sees the change’s shape before the build finishes — Task_ConeReport names what will rebuild and whether a shared hub is touched, posted while the checkout is still running — then gates on Task_Qa by reading the cone’s own rows in the aggregate first. On a PR branch it also deploys the preview itself, but never seeds the shared cache: that stays Lane_PubMgr’s, reached only past Gateway_Path on main or a release. | . | Publication manager — deploy and seed | publication-manager | Reached only past Gateway_Path’s main-or-release branch, never for a PR preview; the one lane allowed to touch the shared cache. Task_Seed writes to a -test branch and verifies a restore from a clean clone before promoting: the verified restore, not the deploy, licenses the shared cache. | .

508.title: Steps
508.content: Every one of the 19 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Restore derived stateTask_Restore | Incremental build (system) | ig-publication | ig-cache restore: the IG’s AST and the Publisher’s terminology cache (input-cache/txcache/). Exit 0 usable, 1 miss, 2 environment error, 3 present but unusable (corrupt or mismatched, such as a moved toolchain). | . | Log the environment error on the beanTask_LogEnvError | FHIR modeller / PR author (person + authoring agent) | todo-manager | Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change’s bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent. | . | Full publisher buildTask_FullBuild | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publication | Exit 1 or 3 from restore: the whole IG is built. Its outputs become the records the next seed writes. | . | Compute the cone of the changeTask_Cone | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | fsh-cone --changed (scripts/fsh-cone.ts) over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out. | . | Post the cone report on the PRTask_ConeReport | PR reviewer / QC reviewer | quality-controlquality-controlquality-control | Review path: the reviewer sees what this change rebuilds — how many artefacts, and whether a hub (a shared RuleSet, CQL library or value set) is touched — before the build finishes. On main it is a log line. | . | Restricted checkout of the backward coneTask_Checkout | Incremental build (system) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | git sparse-checkout of the cone’s files plus sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and the alias files — a median of three files, p90 eleven, measured on the SMART Immunizations IG. | . | SUSHI on the restricted tankTask_Sushi | Incremental build (system) | l3-fhir-authoring | Compile the restricted checkout with SUSHI — the cone’s FSH, not the whole IG. A build optimisation, not a validation shortcut: SUSHI compiling is not conformance, so a green compile goes on to validation rather than standing in for it. | . | Load or reuse the warm contextTask_ContextLoad | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | ig-publicationig-publicationig-publication | The validator’s server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it. | . | Validate the cone (fhir_validate)Task_Validate | Publisher + validator services (JVM) | fhir-validation | Validate the cone’s resources against the warm validator and report the cone that was checked. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with no findings. 509.title: Decisions
509.content: Every one of the 4 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Cache usable?Gateway_Restore | Answered by the exit code of ig-cache restore (Task_Restore): 0 is a usable cache and takes yes, into the cone machinery. 1 (a miss) or 3 (present but unusable) takes no, to the full publisher build, whose outputs become the records the next seed writes. Exit 2 (an environment error — the cache could not be read, which says nothing about whether it is usable) takes environment error: the run stops and the error is logged, so a broken cache store is not hidden behind a slow full build. | yes → Compute the cone of the changeno → Full publisher buildenvironment error → Log the environment error on the bean | . | Valid?Gateway_Valid | Answered by Task_Validate — the cone’s resources checked against the warm validator. yes goes on to re-render the cone’s records. no logs the findings on the change’s bean and returns them to the author. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine and does not take yes. | no → Log findings on the beanyes → Re-render the cone’s records (fhir_narrative · skip lists) | . | QC clean?Gateway_QcPass | Decided in the reviewer’s QC gate (Task_Qa, quality-control) over qa.json, the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes, reading the cone’s rows first. no files each QC finding as a bean, checking for an existing one first, and returns the findings to the author. yes goes on to deploy. | no → File QC findings as beansyes → PR branch, or main / release? | . | PR branch, or main / release?Gateway_Path | Answered by the push that started the process. PR branch is the review path: deploy the preview, which never seeds the shared cache. main / release is the publish path: deploy the site after a human has authorised the release, then seed the cache (Task_Seed).
