1997.doc: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution
1997.title: Health Workforce Education and Training Institution candidate
1997.content: An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. Also called: Health workforce education and training institution . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 2025.title: Facility/Institution Ownership Type candidate
2025.content: Classification for ownership type: • Publicly-owned: Facilities owned or controlled by a governmental unit or a public corporation (where control is defined as the ability to determine the general corporate policy) corresponding to the institutional sector “government units” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • Not-for-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal or social entities created for the purpose of producing goods and services, whose status does not permit them to be a source of income, profit, or other financial gain for the unit(s) that establish, control or finance them, corresponding to the institutional sector “non-profit institutions serving households” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. • For-profit privately-owned: Facilities that are legal entities set up for the purpose of producing goods and services and are capable of generating a profit or other financial gain for their owners corresponding to the institutional sector “non-financial corporations” defined in the System of National Accounts 2008. Also called: Facility/institution ownership type . From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 2047.title: Remuneration candidate
2047.content: Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 2205.title: quality of the evidence
2205.content: In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. Also called: certainty of the evidence, confidence in the estimates of effect . The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout.

Health workforce education and training programmes will often have a numerus clausus that restricts the number of places for a given programme. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 91; PDF page 105). The library ingest of this edition has no Glossary section, so the definition was extracted from the PDF text layer on 2026-10-31 and needs a person to confirm it. The handbook cites its reference 108 for this entry. | Health Workforce Education and Training Institution (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))An established institution that provides education as its main purpose, such as a school, college, university or training centre. Such institutions are normally accredited or sanctioned by the relevant national education authorities or equivalent to award qualifications. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. In practice, for international comparability, any educational institution not managed by a government institution is classified as private. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 90; PDF page 104). 2214.title: F
2214.content: Facility Type candidate Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. 2215.content: Gender candidate Gender refers to the characteristics of women, men, girls and boys that are socially constructed. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. As a social construct, gender varies from society to society and can change over time. Gender is hierarchical and produces inequalities that intersect with other social and economic inequalities. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Facility Type (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. Whether or not an institution is private is therefore a matter of management, not funding. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. Candidate definitions (7) . | International Health Regulations (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))An international legal instrument that is binding on 196 countries across the globe, including all Member States of WHO. Disaggregation based on administrative boundaries down to the first or second subnational level is recommended (depending on the structure of administrative boundaries and the size of subnational territories), without overlaps between the administrative units. Examples for subnational administrative units are states, regions, provinces, counties, and districts. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 93; PDF page 107). Public Health Workforce candidate The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. This workforce comprises diverse and multidisciplinary occupations, from the health as well as other non-health sectors. 2223.title: Q
2223.content: quality of the evidence In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout. 2231.content: activate-accepted-guidance candidate, extracted The point-of-care system carries out the health worker's decisions on decision-support guidance: each accepted action's request becomes active (intent plan or order) and joins the client's CarePlan; a declined action is not written. Input is the guidance and the decisions; output is the transaction Bundle saved. What makes a disagreement adjudicable, the shape its implementations share, why the adjudication LEADS the criterion while the checker's entry is kept beneath it, and the dispensation that records the reason — scoped to a version, never precedent. Process: processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/library/library-core/adopt-methodology-from-source.md . adversarial-code-review candidate, extracted Review a pull request an agent touched by building the strongest case that it is wrong, unsafe, or not what it claims, and record the verdict where the merge gate reads it: one merge-review/v1 file per head, on the merge-reviews state branch, never in the pull request itself. Covers who may review, what the whole-diff scope is, the RED FLAG categories and their evidence rule, the one rebuttal round, overrides, and how a per-head verdict composes with a merge train. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/adversarial-code-review.md . agent-handoff candidate, extracted Governs handing ONE task to an agent in another environment — a local agent with network the cloud session lacks, a sibling on a different machine, anything that cannot read the coordinator's context and that a person may relay to. States who writes which work item, where the receiver reports, what the person pastes (one sentence: work item, branch, repository) and the brief the work item opens with (second person, to the executor), what the receiver checks before acting, who closes, who may grant an exception, and how to recognise and answer the five ways an executor fails. Use when writing a work item for another agent to execute, and as the receiver before acting on one. Triggers on: hand off, handoff, local agent, agy, mac agent, needs network, executor failed, agent went silent, re-hand, "give me a branch and bean for them", relay, the other agent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/agent-handoff.md . agent-memory candidate, extracted Durable memory for a subagent — the three entry labels and what each promises, why entries are authored as graph nodes rather than in the generated file, the injection budget that silently truncates, and archiving as the third state between "reaches everybody" and "deleted". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-memory.md . agent-permissions candidate, extracted Securing what a coding agent may do without asking, from the person who can grant it: the secure-agent-permissions sub-process, run at session start and on demand when an action is denied. Vendor-neutral: the coding agent is a Tool (Claude Code is one; Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and Codex are others), and each Tool's own config format belongs to its adapter, not here. Covers the permissions the harness's processes need, least privilege, how each one is explained before it is granted, how a grant is recorded, and the rules that no grant relaxes: never self-granted, generated projections are CI's, and merging to main is never a standing permission. 2268.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. For the theme: site-chrome/assets/js/docs-ui.js MOVES the theme's own search markup into the action launcher and binds .search, #search-input and .search-label; docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. 2271.content: Jekyll cache: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 5, last: it caches the rendering of what the components above produce. RESTORE: .jekyll-cache, keyed by the theme, the layouts, includes and plugins, Gemfile.lock and the Ruby version, by exact key only. Jekyll invalidates an entry whose source changed, but a template change is not visible to it, which is why the templates are in the key. SAVE: main only — class (c). Owner role: the preview session (CI speed 2). cache node: jekyll-cache. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Jekyll . Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, stated rather than hidden: ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else never reaches it. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. A clean build, a passing suite and every gate can all miss what only rendering the page and looking finds. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge . The site is already live, so a failure here means a published site with a known problem, not a withheld one. The SME inspects the worked case (for decision support) or the cohort and expected vs computed value (for an indicator definition) and renders a domain verdict (pass, fail, or needs-revision) with rationale. 2272.title: K
2272.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the edit, re-pin candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. 2274.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). 2275.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. 2276.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. The options are DERIVED from the graphs this instance declares in <name>.json, read at the time of asking, so an instance that adds a graph gets it in the offer without anybody editing a skill. Never a list typed from memory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_OfferKg . A bean makes the watch durable past the session that opened it: the container is reclaimed, and what survives is the bean. Starting the watcher and recording that it is running are ONE declared step, so the two cannot disagree about whether anything is watching. It notes the watch on the bean rather than claiming it: only Process_BeanOpen claims a bean. The note is idempotent, so re-entering on a later push does not duplicate it. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_CreateReleaseBranch . Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. Not between Gateway_EditorDecision and Task_RecordDecision: Flow_21b runs Task_RecordDecision -> Gateway_EditorDecision, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: A_Frame opens the subprocess on opening-brief's trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached Task_ReviewFindings with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis adopt · hold · decline candidate, extracted On the single edge into PM_Decide, and deliberately not earlier: the MVP build and its gates are HOW the options' costs are measured, so an analysis before Task_Mvp would weigh alternatives against no evidence. Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Organise entry in docs/requirements/index.md by concern group & status candidate, extracted Add or update the requirement's row in docs/requirements/index.md under its canonical concern group (sdlc, process, tools, kg, library, content, ui, conduct from code-lists/concern-group.json) for in-force requirements, or move it to the Superseded and Retired Requirements table when superseded or retired. 2277.content: P1.1 · Agree the terms candidate, extracted The parties agree the purpose, the datasets, the period, the conditions and duties, which trust anchors each side accepts, and the legal basis the sharing rests on (consent, treatment, public-health law or a research waiver). This sets what the text must say; it is a negotiation between people. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_AgreeTerms . P1.2 · Write the legal text candidate, extracted Write the agreement as a document folio: one normative statement per clause the parties must keep, through normative-statements. The text says which governs if it and a machine-readable form disagree (suggested: the text). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_WriteText . P1.2a · Record the legal basis candidate, extracted The text states the legal basis the parties agreed in P1.1 as a normative statement: consent, treatment, public-health law, or a research waiver. Consent rule 1: only an agreement whose legal basis is consent carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty; treatment, public-health law and research waivers do not rest on consent. The gateway that follows, the ODRL and the reviewers all read the basis from this statement. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_RecordLegalBasis . P1.2b · Draft the plain summary candidate, extracted Consent-based only. Write a plain-language summary of the agreement in the same document folio: what it lets the recipient do with the person's data, in words the person can read. Consent rule 3: every agreement that needs consent publishes this summary, hashed with the agreement (P2.2a), and the summary is what the person consents to. It is reviewed, rendered and versioned with the text. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_PlainSummary . P1.3 · Derive the ODRL 2.2 Agreement candidate, extracted Computable only. One assigner and one assignee (ODRL 2.2 §2.1.3), permissions and prohibitions with target assets (§2.2), constraints (§2.5.1) and duties (§2.6.3), written as JSON-LD. Purposes from HL7 PurposeOfUse. Consent rule 1: the Agreement carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty only when the legal basis recorded in P1.2a is consent. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DeriveOdrl . P1.4 · Check the ODRL against the text candidate, extracted Computable only. A person checks that the ODRL says what the text says, and signs it off. A program can check the ODRL is well formed; it cannot check that it matches the text. The check includes the consent duty: present when the legal basis is consent, absent otherwise (consent rule 1). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CheckOdrl . P1.5 · Split public terms from private annexes candidate, extracted Split the agreement into a public template and private annexes (security controls, named staff). Only the hash of a private annex is ever published. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SplitAnnexes . P1.6 · Sign candidate, extracted The signatories sign: wet ink, or an electronic signature under national law. Technically a detached JWS (RFC 7515) or CMS (RFC 5652); PAdES for a signed PDF needs the owner's approval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Sign . P14.2 · Decide what happens to existing grants candidate, extracted Existing grants keep citing the old hash. The parties decide, per agreement: they stay valid until expiry, or they are revoked and reissued against the new version (in smart-trust). The old version stays readable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DecideGrants . P14.3 · New consent needed candidate, extracted The amendment widens use, so a Consent citing the old version's URL and hash does not cover the new version (consent rule 2). Record on the bean, and in the new version's text, that new consent is needed; the new version gets its own plain-language summary (P1.2b). Asking each person again is the trust layer's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_NewConsentNeeded . P14.5 · Set the status to ended candidate, extracted Set the life-cycle status of the agreement's DCAT 3 record (DCAT 3 §6.4.30). The published versions stay readable at their URLs. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_SetStatus . P2.1 · Assign version and fixed URL candidate, extracted Each signed version gets its own immutable URL (for example /dsa/42/v3). A 'latest' URL may exist; nothing cites it. A new version never overwrites an old one. This fixed-version URL is the one a Consent cites (consent rule 2), and a computable agreement's ODRL policy uid is set to it (P2.3). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_AssignVersion . P2.2 · Record each file's SHA-256 candidate, extracted Compute SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of the signed text, and of the ODRL file if there is one, recorded as DCAT 3 spdx:checksum and verified by check:dsa-hash. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Hash . P2.2a · Hash the plain summary candidate, extracted Consent-based only. Record the SHA-256 of the plain-language summary beside the agreement's, in the same version (consent rule 3). The summary a person consented to can then be checked against the agreement it summarises; a changed summary is a new version. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_HashSummary . P2.2b · State the URL and hash to cite candidate, extracted Consent-based only. The version's publication metadata states the fixed-version URL (P2.1) and the hash (P2.2) that a Consent cites in FHIR R4 Consent.policy.uri (consent rule 2), never the 'latest' URL. For a computable agreement that URL is also the ODRL policy uid (P2.3): a Consent counts only when its Consent.policy.uri equals the agreement's ODRL policy uid, so the two are the same string. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConsentCitation . P2.3 · Make the ODRL cite the text candidate, extracted The ODRL policy names the signed text distribution with dcterms:source (DCMI Terms), pointing at the immutable URL whose spdx:checksum was just recorded. Its uid is that same fixed-version URL, the URL a Consent cites in Consent.policy.uri (consent rule 2). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_OdrlCitesText . P2.4–5 · Write the DCAT 3 record candidate, extracted One DCAT 3 record: the agreement as a catalogued resource, each file a dcat:Distribution with dcat:downloadURL and spdx:checksum; datasets it covers carry odrl:hasPolicy. Versions are linked with DCAT 3 versioning (previous version, version, current version). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Catalogue . Package with digests candidate, extracted The serialization alone is not a package. A package is an addressable set — the JSON-LD, the assets it references, and a manifest naming every file with its digest and byte count. The manifest is what makes a REMOVED file detectable, which a per-file signature cannot do on its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Package . Persist the log to the data store candidate, extracted Capture is explicitly on — by <cat-harness.processes:log capture="on"/> on the process or by config — so the entries go to the git data store. Only this branch commits anything. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_PersistLog . Personas and roles [l2-dak-authoring] candidate, extracted Persona and actor-definition blocks; organisational roles and governance bodies get their own kind once it exists. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Call_Personas . Personas and scenarios candidate, extracted Author the DAK's personas and the user scenarios they appear in. Calls Process_L2ComponentEditReview with the personas-and-scenarios inputs of the skill l2-component-edit-review (checker: dak-swimlanes.ts and traceability to L1 recommendations; renderer: the persona card and a prose diff; reviewer: clinical SME). These are the DAK's own actors, not this harness's scenarios/roles.json; do not conflate the two. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_Personas . Phase 1 Needs candidate, extracted Identify the stakeholders, synthesise a needs statement from the sources, and loop until the BA and the stakeholders both recognise it. The loop is the phase: a needs statement nobody confirmed is an agent's summary, not a requirement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Needs . Phase 1: Identify stakeholders candidate, extracted The agent asks the BA who is affected by this change. The BA knows the domain — the agent does not guess. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Stakeholders . Phase 1: Synthesise needs from sources candidate, extracted From the chat, issue, uploads and library sources, write a clear, jargon-free statement of what is needed and why, tied to a concrete workflow. Post it on the GitHub issue, not in chat, and ask the requester and stakeholders to review it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Synthesise . Phase 2: Map current workflow (BPA) candidate, extracted Business-process analysis here means reading the existing diagrams under processes/ and drawing the gap, so the skill that implements this step is the BPMN one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_MapWorkflow . Phase 4a: Compare the viable options candidate, extracted Phase 4 often ends with a CHOICE rather than a plan, and this is the step that hands it over. Per option: what it does, its pro, its con, what it changes DOWNSTREAM, and how reversible it is — laid out where the rows can be read against each other, then one recommendation and a stated default. A step of its own rather than a line inside A_DefineReqs, because it has a different output and a different reader: the impact analysis is for the record, the comparison is the thing the BA answers from. Folding it in is how it gets skipped — the analysis feels finished, so the options go over as a list of names. When Call_Wireframe ran, its wireframe candidates are among the options: one row per candidate, with a link to its web and mobile screenshots. Skipped legitimately when the analysis yields ONE viable approach. Do not manufacture alternatives to fill a table. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_CompareOptions . Phase 5 Plan + sign-off candidate, extracted The approved requirements become work-plan items, the BA signs off, and the branch is announced on the issue. The announcement is on the single edge into delivery, so the three loops back into implementation do not re-announce. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Signoff . Phase 5: Create beans candidate, extracted The agent mints the implementation beans itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first. The engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean — so what this step records here is a note that the plan now exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_CreateBeans . Phase 6 Implement + acceptance candidate, extracted One phase and not three, because the loops say so: an increment the BA rejects, an MVP that is not ready, and stakeholder findings all route back into implementation. A subprocess has one exit and cannot be re-entered once finished, so splitting this region would have changed what the diagram says. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Deliver . Phase 6: Implement (feature branch + PR) candidate, extracted Inner loop: agent claims a bean, implements on feature branch, opens PR, posts summary to the issue. When the requirement changes a rendered surface, implement against the wireframe candidate the requester or BA chose in Phases 3–4 (Process_WireframeDesignReview, called from Process_CRDM_Requirements), not against a fresh design; and the delivery summary links the chosen candidate beside the after-screenshot, so the reviewer can see the build matches what was approved. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_Implement . Phases 2–4 BPA + requirements candidate, extracted Map the current workflow, then define the requirements and the impact they carry, and loop until approved. Same shape as Phase 1 and for the same reason: an unapproved requirement is a proposal. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Requirements . Phases 3–4: Define requirements + impact candidate, extracted Two skills, because this step is two things: the requirements come from the CRDM process, the impact half is a question about the entities and relations the change touches, which is what data modelling answers; a folio-content skill such as content-graph is not one this harness diagram can bind. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_DefineReqs . Pick up the stale pin candidate, extracted The hand-off from the mechanical lane to the one that can exercise judgement. Claiming the bean here is what stops two sessions adopting the same bump. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-pin-watch.bpmn#A_PickUp . Place by ownership; declare the directory candidate, extracted A domain-neutral method belongs to the harness and a domain method to the folio that owns the domain. If the session cannot write where it belongs, draft it where it can, say so in the file, and open a bean to move it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Place . Place it by hand, with a reason candidate, extracted Recorded as a queue entry whose placement is override with a position and a reason; the schema refuses one without a reason. It enters the next placement as the table's ownerOverride input. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Override . Place it in uploads/ by a declared route candidate, extracted THE FIRST LINK: everything downstream of here takes a file that is already in the queue, so without this step how the file got there is governed by nothing. WHAT THIS STEP IS. The basic flow's ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the instance that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. 2278.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA gate: review dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_QaGate . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Report . QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-quality-gates.bpmn#Task_QaWorkingCopy . QC gates candidate, extracted The QC reviewer rules on the aggregate QA against the publication gates. Emitting the QA report is mechanical; ruling on it is the reviewer's decision. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_QcGates . Quarantine and report the mismatch candidate, extracted Not published, not retried silently. The record keeps its reference to IRIS and the bitstream is marked unknown. BPMN activities of who-iris · source who-iris/processes/iris-cdn-initial-load.bpmn#Task_Quarantine . Query data repositories and statistical datasets candidate, extracted Indicator and microdata sources. Distinct from the two above because the unit of evidence is a MEASUREMENT with a population, a period and a method, not a claim in prose. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/evidence-retrieval.bpmn#Task_DataRepos . Queue prose blocks for summary candidate, extracted A QA sidecar of general document ingestion, drained slowly. Nothing is written to ENQUEUE a block: the queue is derived (every prose block in every declared library, minus those whose summaries.json record is a current draft or confirmation), so a promoted entry is in it the moment its blocks are. A re-ingested document whose text changed re-enters it on its own, because the record's source_hash no longer matches. What an agent doing ingestion work does here is DRAIN a few: bun run cat summaries:next -- --n K hands it the next K blocks with their text, it writes a short summary of each in its own words, and bun run cat summaries:record writes them into library/<bib-slug>/summaries.json as drafts naming the agent and its model. The block itself stays verbatim and ingested. ADVISORY, never a gate: this step does not hold up Task_Citeable, and check:l1-complete reports the backlog (block-summaries) without failing on it. Confirming or rejecting a draft is a person's act, in bun run cat narratives. 2280.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, R–Z
2280.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 630 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 49 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 250 (SKOS) · smart-base 159 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 422 terms and is 336 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 1124 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 1124 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 422 shown . R S T U V W

2281.title: R
2281.content: Raise a finding against the wrong side candidate, extracted The prose and the code really disagree: raise a finding that names which side is wrong and why. Usually the prose, because the code is what runs — but a skill can state intended behaviour correctly while the code has regressed, and then the finding is against the code. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_RaiseFinding . Raise findings before the assets land candidate, extracted Findings go back to whoever authored the choice, because the choice was theirs: a theme is picked per note by a human or an agent, and there is no mapping to correct instead. Raised, never silently fixed — a reviewer who re-themes a note has substituted their judgement for the author's without saying so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_RaiseFindings . Never return silent partial answers. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/named-query-execution.bpmn#A_RaiseMissingPartition . Z-order is session-only by stated default: no z is written to the layout, so a raise is never a file write. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_Raise . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Retrain . The sweep runs daily and proposes; this acts. Between them a branch can come back to life — bean w2g5 documents exactly that, a session reusing one branch across five successive pull requests. Says agree, disagree or unknown; unknown (could not run) is said as plainly as a disagreement, because the table reads both the same way and an unknown read as agreement certifies on one party's word. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_ReExecuteSample . Re-materialize and record new fixity candidate, extracted The gates are re-asked, not inherited: a licence can change, and a collection can grow past the size a caller agreed to. AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Apply . Re-pin downstream mounts, as PRs candidate, extracted For each instance whose index.config.json mounts this repository: a PR moving ref to the merge commit, with a trust.consent whose evidence quotes the owner's consent to that pin, and the lock regenerated by mount:remote. Each re-pin PR is itself a merge to main and runs this process again. When the re-pin moves a layer whose software-library nodes are derived at the pin (bootstrap-tools, whose nodes cat-harness-tools holds in libraries/held/), the same PR runs bun run cat libraries:derive, and libraries:check fails until it does (owner, 2026-10-30, bootstrap-tools#44). None found is recorded with where it looked. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Repin . Re-read the prose against the code candidate, extracted For each open item, read the prose claim beside the code it describes and decide what is true. For a stale pair, read what changed in the code and whether the prose still describes it. For an undetermined claim, say whether it points at something real outside this repository. For a false claim, check the checker's reading before trusting it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_ReRead . Re-render the agent surface candidate, extracted When the lock changed, the layers an agent's skills and memory are generated from changed with it. mount:remote re-runs the generators of what an agent actually reads — skill:commands (.claude/commands/) and agent-memory (.claude/agent-memory/ and the .agents/ copies) — from the checkout root, and a generator that fails fails the run. A re-pin commit therefore carries the new layers AND the surface rendered from them, because new layers shipped without their rendered surface fail the agent-memory tests. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_RenderAgentSurface . Moves the change-set to another TWG review committee and records who, when, from, to and why on the change-set record, so re-ingesting comments never resets it. Person-only (userTask): agents cannot re-route a change-set on their own. Not drift: synonyms, articles, word order, inflection, a purpose clause rendered in the subjunctive, an acronym left uninflected, an acronym spelled out with the acronym kept. Drift: a claim added, dropped, weakened, strengthened or reversed; a term of art swapped for one that means something else; a named entity, number or quantifier moved. Read each queued PR's live facts candidate, extracted From GitHub and the checkout, now: authored paths, shared declarations, size, conflict risk and overlap KIND against the other queued PRs (T3), own CI and whether it ran on the head (T2). Tools: merge:overlap for the overlap facts, check:head-has-run for ownCi. Nothing read here is written to a queue entry; it is the input to the placement table. ownCi IS NOT A VERDICT READ. Never ask whether anything is red: ask which workflow runs are OWED for the head's event and whether each one is present and successful. The two readings come apart, measured 2026-10-02 on #1889's head 7ab6119405 -- 9 runs present, all 9 gating job NAMES matching, 3 of them in_progress with a null conclusion, and 3 check SUITES completed as action_required having executed nothing. A filter for conclusion = failure finds zero, and counting the runs does not catch it either. check:head-has-run is the only thing here that asks the owed question (bean 3pqn), and the five states it distinguishes are the five values of ownCi. Rule_HeadNotGreen in merge-priority.dmn then hands back anything but green, so this is a gate the engine applies rather than advice a steward remembers. Overlap kind matters as much as overlap: merge:overlap over all 36 open PRs on 2026-10-02 (459 pairs) found #1907 x #1909 NOT independent on package.json alone, with zero authored content shared. generated-only needs a regeneration and shared-declaration needs ordering; only authored needs a train. WHICH ITEMS: named by the source's identifiers, or by a subset strategy its descriptor supports. WHICH STORE: the knowledge graph or other structured store the import is tested against. PERMANENT OR TRIAL: a permanent sample lands in library/ and is refreshed; a trial lands in fsh-guts/ and is not. Scrap with reasons NEVER delete candidate, extracted status: scrapped, plus a "Reasons for Scrapping" section. This is what "disable" means here — the CLI has no disabled state; its vocabulary is draft, todo, in-progress, completed, scrapped. The agent's own beans update; the engine has no scrap op. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. They compose; composing them is the safer and more expensive default, and it is the deployment's choice rather than the pipeline's.
