A title already known for the document (the catalogue's dc.title, or one given with --title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections' doc_title does not carry a scan's misreading. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_Structure . Write the announcement, with links candidate, extracted A short communication for the public: what is under review, the comment period, a high-level description of the process, and links to the release, every channel and the published process. Skills: public-comment-channels, public-comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_WriteAnnouncement . Write the BagIt tag files (sorted, no dates) candidate, extracted scripts/iris-cdn/bag.ts tagFiles: manifest-sha256.txt sorted by path, bag-info.txt with Payload-Oxum and no Bagging-Date. BPMN activities of who-iris · source who-iris/processes/iris-cdn-sign-publish.bpmn#Task_BuildBag . Write the change set's Agent row candidate, extracted On the Agent tab, the change set's row: Agentic status (Not started, Working, PR open, Ready for review, Change merged or Needs human); Pull request; Staging review page; Staging built, PR head, Staging built from and Staging deploy from agent-record.ts push; and Agent step from agent-record.ts step <name>, exactly "<step> <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ>" with a step from the fixed list (reading, proposing, editing, pushing, staging, deploying, qa-review, merging, proposed, idle). Prose in Agent step is not read: use idle when the row waits for people. A preview or review link is written only once it is live: the GitHub Pages deploy of a gh-pages commit at or after the preview's publish has succeeded, and an HTTP GET of each link answers 200 where the agent can reach the site. A publish that is only on the gh-pages branch is not live: Pages deploys can be queued for many minutes or cancelled by the next push. Until then Staging review page stays empty, Staging deploy says deploying, and Feedback (agent) says "Preview deploying" with no preview link. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/record-agent-step.bpmn#Task_WriteAgentRow . Write the design intent candidate, extracted A short statement of who the screen is for, what they need to do, and what it must show. It is the criterion every candidate is judged against. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Intent . Write the entry and cache the declaration candidate, extracted The subscriptions entry in the subscriber's instance declaration — id, repository, ref, and nothing chosen yet — plus a cached copy of the substrate's declaration at the pin. The entry holds the choice and the pin, never state: whether a part is held is answered by its materialisation record, and a second answer here would be free to disagree with it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Record . Write the entry that LEADS — keeping the checker's beneath it candidate, extracted Not relaxable, and the one step here that is not. A judgement nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from a checker that was never run, so the judgement is free and the record is not. Do not resolve the disagreement away: both entries stay, the adjudication on top under the sweep's most-recent-matching-hash rule. A disagreement between a checker and a reviewer is information, and somebody re-running the check next month needs to find that a checker read it differently rather than a clean pass. /api/relevance/adjudicate reached the same rule independently — human_adjudicated written alongside, never over, the agent's assessed_by. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_RecordEntry . Write the generated-data recipe candidate, extracted Record contentType, specialisation, template, params, seed, and the canonical sha256 digest (computeGeneratedSetDigest) with $schema: "test-data-generated/1.0.0" and kind: "generated" in the instance's declared test-data-generated directory. Never store materialised records. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-data-curation.bpmn#Task_WriteRecipe . Write the locale's QA report candidate, extracted One report per locale under test/results/translation-qa/: coverage, the gates, the round trip with its counts and every drift ruling, the glossary violations and sense checks, and the source errors reported. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_QAReport . Write the lock candidate, extracted index.lock.json beside the downstream's index.config.json (the legacy <instance>.mount-lock.json is still read, and is renamed onto the new name when rewritten; both present is an error): the pins it was written for, each instance's repository, SHA and how the pin was found, each directory's tree digest — and what was NOT mounted, with why, so an offline check cannot read a gap as clean. Whoever writes the lock writes its layers cache ref (layers:publish, which refuses unless every mount hashes to the lock); on main, the index's workflow does it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_WriteLock . Write the note into the folio — with no coordinate candidate, extracted A new note: write it into the folio with no x, no y, no board and no position. A folio is complete with no board, and one note may sit on several boards, which a coordinate on the note could not express. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-place-note.bpmn#A_CreateNote . Write the root README, if it is not there candidate, extracted The repository now IS an instance of something, and nothing at its root says so. It carries a LINK to the harness that was installed and the OVERALL install status across every location — WHEN ABSENT, never replacing: where a README is already there, the link and status go in a marker pair the harness's own README tool maintains. Initialization may create the README: the rule that a running process never writes an instance-readme governs an instance that already exists. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_WriteRootReadme . Write the slice definition candidate, extracted Add one SliceDef to the builder's slice table: the DDL (one table per node type, edge tables, one CONTENTLESS full-detail FTS5), the order each table's rows go in, the load that turns the source into rows, where the payloads live (written at deploy, or already published), and the search block the generic page reads. Choose the heavy fields by kg-export §"What is heavy": a heavy field is a payload_sha256 pointer, never a stored column. Never copy the builder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Define . Write the test run and the test report candidate, extracted The run records plan {id, version} and sut {actor, version, reach} with its data and process hashes; the report rolls up per plan, never across plans, and goes to the qa-reports branch at tests/plan/sut/run/. No verdict in it may name the system under test as its reviewer. Writes a folio-test-run/v1 and a test-report/v1. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_WriteRun . Write what changed candidate, extracted An instance opened or closed, a bean claimed, a wait started or ended. All by REFERENCE: the bean and the instance are each the authority on themselves, and a status copied here would be free to contradict them. NO cat-harness.processes:bean on this step. It records that a claim happened; it does not claim. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_UpdateSession .

2288.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
2288.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 630 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 49 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 250 (SKOS) · smart-base 159 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 381 terms and is 302 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 1124 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 1124 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 381 shown . 0–9 A B C D

2289.content: 0 · Describe the use case candidate, extracted Population, setting, jurisdiction, interventions in scope. The user's own words; the agent asks a numbered question if the request did not say. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_DescribeUseCase . 0 · Scope the DTH and place it in the DIIG [content-plan] candidate, extracted Name the health-system area, the audience and the DIIG phase the handbook supports, citing the one DIIG phase figure (DIIG section 1.1, Figure 1.1.1). Decide which DTHs and which smart-ra content it builds on. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Scope . 1 · Declare in place (nothing moves) candidate, extracted A <name>.json entry with its graphs[] kinds. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Declare . 1 · Declare it in place, with its seam candidate, extracted <name>/<name>.json with name, version, repository (the planned home), livesAt (where it sits today), needs, and only the directories that exist, each declared with its files in one commit. <name>/platform.ts from the first commit, so no climb out of the directory ever needs rerouting. Scaffolded by init-folio --staged <path>, which writes those two files and nothing at the host root; never --instance, which writes a whole repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Declare . 1 · Identify L1 guidelines and recommendations candidate, extracted Component 1 sources of any DAK already in scope first, then WHO IRIS and the jurisdiction's own guidelines. Each candidate marked in-library / in-KG / not yet. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_IdentifyL1 . 1 · Ingest sources into library/ [library-ingestion] candidate, extracted Every source as received, frozen: WHO publications through who-iris, the TWG outline and workbooks from uploads/. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Ingest . 1–3 · Declare, detangle, isolate candidate, extracted The graph-detanglement practice, all of its gates: declared in place, zero wrong-direction edges on every axis, and standing alone with its own declaration, namespace and artefact. A plain task on purpose, not a call to graph-detanglement.bpmn: that process ends in its own authorise-and-extract steps, which here are stages 9-13 of this one, and calling it would run them twice. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Detangle . 10 · Re-point: livesAt, seam, mount or subscription candidate, extracted In the new repository livesAt goes (absent means it sits at the root of repository) and platform.ts points at where the platform now is. The host consumes it as a remote mount (a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json) if it imports its code, or a subscription if it only reads its content, pinned to a commit while staging. Additive: the host keeps its copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Repoint . 10 · Seed both repositories candidate, extracted Seed main, then bring the content and the tools in as reviewed pull requests with their history, so neither repository's first commit is unreviewable. The seed includes every publisher the declaration promises (sub-kg-lifecycle stage 10): a qa directory with storage needs .github/workflows/publish-qa.yml, the caller of the tools layer's layer-qa-publish.yml, and test/results/ ignored. Without it the declared store is never written, and once the layer stops committing its results no reader finds them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Seed . 11 · Parent consumes, additively candidate, extracted The parent pins the pair (a commit while staging, a version once released) — a code dependency as a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json (remote-mount skill), never a submodule — repoints its imports, and keeps its own copy until it is green with the dependency declared. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Consume . 11 · Verify on a fresh clone candidate, extracted bun run cat sub-kg:verify-clone --repo <owner>/<name> --ref <branch> (Tool sub-kg-verify-clone): clone into an empty scratch directory with submodules and any sibling it needs, install, and run its own gates. Green, red or unknown, and unknown is never green. Nothing in a seed runs standalone until the seam is re-pointed, so a missing module shows here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_FreshClone . 12 · First release candidate, extracted Tag each repository, publish /v<major>/. From here the two are versioned independently; a tools release lists the content majors it supports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Release . 12 · Owner confirms: freeze the in-repo copy candidate, extracted The agent reports the files that would move, their size, the new repository and the commit the copy matches, then asks: (1) freeze it in the kept trashcan now, (2) keep in place until the first release, (3) show the file list first. Default if there is no answer: (2), nothing moves. A green fresh clone is the precondition for asking, not the answer. Non-relaxable. The host keeps a FROZEN copy in the kept trashcan, not a refreshed mirror and not a deletion; the live copy is the remote mount or subscription set up at stage 10. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConfirmCutover . 13 · Cutover: freeze the copy in the kept trashcan candidate, extracted Only on the owner's answer (1) at step 12. The in-repo directory moves, as one relocation, under separated/<name>/ in the kept trashcan, on its own branch (a plain mv, git rm --cached, state:push; the trashcan skill says how), with ONE note carrying movedFrom, movedOn, the new repository and the commit the copy matches. Frozen: never refreshed, never rendered; a reader wanting the live content follows the note to the new repository. On main this is one revertable commit removing the directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Cutover . 13 · Cutover: retire the parent's copy candidate, extracted The one commit worth reverting, made only after the parent consumes the release and every identifier dereferences. It retires the parent's copy, frozen, never refreshed and never rendered, rather than deleting it. Where the copy goes is the sub-kg-lifecycle skill's stage 13; this diagram does not name that store, because the published graph must not. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Cutover . 2 · Grow it in place candidate, extracted The content type's own authoring process runs here, against the staged instance. Many sub-KGs never leave; this task can last as long as the graph does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Grow . 2 · Ingest into the L1 KG candidate, extracted Per source not yet extracted: cat ingest into library/, the generic-document layer (l1-library), then the L1 layer (recommendations, remarks, practices, scenario candidates) into library/<bib>/l1-extraction/. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_IngestKg . 2 · Outline chapters against the dth kind [document-structure] candidate, extracted Map the outline onto the dth document kind's sections and report every required section that is missing. dth-hrh's build_from_outline.py is the only instance; there is no general outline seed. Placeholder: no platform subprocess; done by hand, as for dth-hrh. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Outline . 2a · Measure — unassigned column FIRST candidate, extracted bun run cat check:partition. Read the unassigned column before the edge count, and quote BOTH numbers rather than only the one that improved. The edge count can rise when the measurement improves (previously unjudged edges are folded in); that is correct. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Measure . 2b · Prune, merge, factor — or the classification is wrong candidate, extracted The only four moves. Move the shared TARGET first and the importers after; check the target's layer before the importer's; a schema moves with its script. The fix is never an exemption, it is the right owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Move . 3 · Choose L2 dependencies (WHO / jurisdiction DAKs) candidate, extracted From the L1 KG: which existing DAKs to reuse, adapt, extend or reject, each with evidence and reason. Reuse first; prefer the jurisdiction's adaptation, recording the WHO original as its upstream. For each component kept, record how the candidate produces it (the tools graph, the candidate repository's source spreadsheets and converters, WHO's DAK toolchain); stage 4 uses that toolchain. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_DepsL2 . 3 · Isolate — own declaration, namespace, artefact candidate, extracted Only once cross-edges measure zero: give the sub-graph its own declaration, its own namespace and its own published artefact, as bootstrap/ has (its own declaration, bs: namespace and graph document). Nothing moves yet; the sub-graph now stands alone in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Isolate . 3 · Push generic down first candidate, extracted Move what is generic into the harness below before the seam is closed, and consolidate what the sub-KG needs into the harness it instantiates. Wrong-direction edges hide in declarations and data as well as imports: run check:import-direction, check:reference-direction and check:process-bindings. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_PushDown . 4 · Comment via contributor log sheet or GitHub pc: [content-feedback] candidate, extracted The contributor log (Google Sheet) and pc: lines on GitHub issues and PRs. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Comments . 4 · Create / adapt L2 DAK assets candidate, extracted The authoring steps of l2-dak-authoring.bpmn (personas and scenarios, BPMN, DMN, data dictionary, indicators and requirements, terminology), plus the design of each data-entry form as wireframe candidates (wireframe-design-review, design use) from the persona, the user scenario and the core data elements. Its clinical validation is this stage's adjudication and does not hold up stage 5. The IG is built through fhir-harness's AST cache lifecycle (ig-ast-refresh.yml), with the DAK pre-processing as smart-base's pre-export overlay (dak-preprocessing, dak-pre-export.sh) and the DAK sidecars made from the AST (dak-postprocessing). BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_L2 . 4 · Extract — a directory move, not a file-by-file sift candidate, extracted Only once edges are zero and the declaration stands alone: move the sub-graph out as one directory move, not a file-by-file sift. Its nested declaration resolves paths against its own directory, so moving the folder moves the graph. The five-point gate is in migration-plan.md Phase II. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Extract . 4 · Identity: version, iriBase, nodeSchemas candidate, extracted The declaration carries name, version, iriBase, needs and nodeSchemas. A base move is bun run iri:sync -- --from <old base>, once; then iri:sync:check and check:node-iris are green. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Identity . 4 · Route every climb through platform.ts candidate, extracted Every platform symbol the sub-KG uses is re-exported from <name>/platform.ts, so re-pointing the platform is a one-file edit. A merge from main is where new climbs arrive; reroute them here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seam . 5 · Choose L3 dependencies (WHO / jurisdiction IGs) candidate, extracted Index each candidate IG, then match the L1 KG and the L2 assets against it: reuse, adapt, extend or reject per IG, and record per artefact type the candidate's toolchain (CQL refresh, test-case format, example generator), which stage 6 then uses. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_DepsL3 . 5 · Move harness output about it to the host candidate, extracted QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository's, published to that repository's qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Hosted . 5 · Open public comment [public-comment] candidate, extracted A separate store, review/public-comment, and the public-comment review sheet. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_OpenPublic . 5 · Rehearse self-contained candidate, extracted bun run cat seed:ready --layer <name> --rehearse copies the layer and what it needs into a scratch workspace of sibling directories and runs the tests there. Run the gates rather than scanning imports: a static scan misses files the gates load at run time, and renaming the directory changes every generated page. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . 6 · Editorial, voice and translation QA [quality-control] candidate, extracted The DTH voice (smart-base skills/voices/who-digital-transformation-handbook), figures and translations. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/dth-authoring.bpmn#Task_Qa . 6 · Produce L3 assets candidate, extracted The mapping and pipeline of dak-l3-ig.bpmn, up to a clean IG build. Every L3 asset names the L2 asset it implements in wasDerivedFrom, with that edge's adjudication state. Each Questionnaire is derived from the chosen L2 wireframe of its form. Publication continues in that process and is not on the path to stage 8. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_L3 . 6 · Report what would move, and how it undoes candidate, extracted Before the first outward-facing step the agent reports: the files and bytes that would move, the history that comes with them, what in the host changes, and how each step is undone. It never creates a repository on its own initiative. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Report . 6 · Split content from tools candidate, extracted Create <name>-tools as a sibling directory and move the code: the Zod source, the generators, the README and diagram writers, the content checks. Cut its import cone to its own files and declared packages. Both start at the content's version. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Split . 7 · L4: describe the consuming application candidate, extracted Who uses it, on what device, which L2 processes and L3 resources it covers, connectivity, the systems it talks to. The agent offers options drawn from the L2 personas and processes. This is the written intent wireframe-design-review starts from. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_DescribeApp . 7 · Owner confirms: create the repository candidate, extracted Creating a repository is visible outside this one and is not undone by a revert. Numbered options, recommended first: (1) the owner creates it and says when it exists, (2) the agent creates it, only with that permission, (3) not yet. Default if there is no answer: (3), nothing is created. Non-relaxable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConfirmCreate . 7 · Plan publication candidate, extracted Every identifier the content mints is a file some step publishes: /v<major>/, for what programs read and pages people read alike; the exact release is the pin's. Name collisions between published files are resolved here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Plan . 8 · Create the repository candidate, extracted The owner creates the repository, or authorises the agent that has the permission to; when that agent is in another environment, the hand-over is one work item and one sentence (agent-handoff). The new repository is read before anything is written to it: empty is a fact to check, not to assume. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . 8 · Rehearse standalone candidate, extracted Copy the content and the tools alone into a temporary directory, with nothing else on the path, and run the tools' checks there. An empty tree must exit non-zero, so a rehearsal over nothing cannot pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . 8a · L4: wireframe the application candidate, extracted To-be mode, from the stage-7 intent: two or more candidates, web and mobile, with real content from the L2 personas and scenarios. The agent goes on with its recommended candidate; the requester may choose another during adjudication. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_WireframeApp . 8b · L4: build the consuming application candidate, extracted Against the stage-6 IG build, with conformance tests from the IG's examples and test cases. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/smart-guideline-end-to-end.bpmn#Task_BuildApp . 9 · Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. Declining leaves the graph declared, detangled, isolated and split in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Authorise . 9 · Copy the staged contents in, with history candidate, extracted git subtree split --prefix=<name> in the host, then the split branch added to the new repository on a branch, as a draft pull request, never straight to main. The new repository's own root files are a second commit, so the copy stays byte-identical and reviewable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seed .

2290.title: A
2290.content: Abort, restore the tree, list what was refused candidate, extracted git merge --abort. Each refused path is listed with its pattern's reason, or "no declared pattern". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Abort . Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Asking for the upload first demands the one thing they may not have, before the cheaper answers have been offered. Say what happens if they do nothing. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Task_AskReview . Lead with what changed in prose, then the links, the before/after and the checker's findings; put the question in interaction-modality's form. Post it where the work is discussed (this conversation, the originating GitHub issue, the pull request), with the same links in each. A comment tagged on the PR becomes a review-comment todo (review-comments). BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-component-edit-review.bpmn#Task_RequestReview . Ask ONE question candidate, extracted One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Asked through the one reusable discussion, with the exact step written out so it can be followed without opening anything else. A person saying "done" is recorded as their word, not as a check; the next run checks it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_AskPerson . A head younger than 15 minutes legitimately has no run yet and is skipped. Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 could not determine; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-determine. Where its verdict comes from: Asked of the verdict output of the Sweep step in .github/workflows/pr-checks-present.yml, which runs check:prs-have-runs --min-age-minutes 15. Exit 0 is clean, 1 findings, 2 could not determine; an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is reclassified as could-not-determine, as is any other code. no is verdict == 'unknown': 'Refuse to report success on an unchecked repository' runs exit 1 and the tracking issue is left untouched. yes is verdict != 'unknown', the guard on ensuring the pr-no-checks label. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme's subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term's translation; an instance layer only adds. A match in another subject area is a sense check, not a violation. Each layer's glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. A fixed translation is an authored term with a non-empty, non-fuzzy msgstr in its scheme's catalogue. Record the measurement in the work context with its provenance (the command and the date), beside the size of the source it replaces. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Measure . Build staging site candidate, extracted feature-staging.yml triggers: 1. Regenerate docs (schema, skills, content-backed pages) 2. Render BPMN diagrams 3. Stamp build with commit SHA + timestamp + branch 4. Build Jekyll site with branches/ baseurl 5. Inject yellow staging banner into every HTML page A draft pull request is staged too, from its first push. A build takes about 22 minutes, and GitHub Pages about 3 to 4 more. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_BuildStaging . Build the docs site candidate, extracted Build the preview from the PR's head: regenerate the generated docs, trim what this preview does not need, render the BPMN diagrams, then Jekyll, TypeDoc and the knowledge-graph export, with the staging banner and SEO identity claims stripped. It is a PREVIEW build (CAT_BUILD_TYPE=preview, owner 2026-11-01): only what the change reaches, and every whole-corpus index (builtAtPublish entries marked index: true, and the search index) is main's copy, put back rather than rebuilt. A branch frozen for public comment is dispatched with build_type: full instead. Skill feature-staging, section Build types. A PREVIEW REBUILDS ONLY ITS DEPENDENCY CONE (owner cards Q-CONE-1 C and Q-CONE-2 B, 2026-11-01): main's writer records say what each derive:publish writer and each step of the QA working copy READ. A writer or QA step whose recorded reads all match is not run, and main's outputs for it are put back. Every other one runs. QA is not left out of a preview, only narrowed to what the change can reach. Inside a preview's QA build, skill:register also leaves to derive:publish the two pages that derive:publish builds anyway and that no later QA step reads (skills:docs and lsi:viz), so they are built once. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Build . Build the draft publication candidate, extracted Render the corpus into the draft form of the folio: PDF, HTML site, or FHIR IG. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_BuildDraft . Build the entry candidate, extracted First the working copy is produced (qa:refresh, bean 3hk4): while the checkout still tracks test/results/, the commit's own copy is the record and nothing runs; once it does not, every declared QA writer runs into the empty tree, because the gates are in judge mode and wrote nothing a publish could carry. A refresh that leaves a writer failed, a family empty or a file unclaimed is INCOMPLETE: the job goes red and qa:publish --completeness refuses, so a partial tree is never stored as the commit's record — the "Not stored" outcome, reached before any push. Then it hashes the working copy of every declared qa directory (<instance>/test/results/**, byte-identical to the checkout's layout) into a tree through a private index, and writes manifest.json (qa-reports-manifest/v1): inputs, producers, verdict counts and the gates' result. Identical JSON is the same blob, so an unchanged family costs nothing to store again. Its git objects live in a private bare repository, never in the checkout's own store. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_BuildEntry . Build the graph partitions candidate, extracted The platform process nquads-distribution (cat-harness): spine plus one partition per community, zero blank nodes, sorted N-Quads. Build the IG with the AST exporter candidate, extracted The runner mounts the layers the IG repository's index.lock.json pins, then restores and judges the cache itself. When it is not valid (or force is set) it rebuilds with the Publisher fork (Tool ig-ast-export, litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher at the pinned claude/ast-export commit). A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller's optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit's input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). The AST just built must itself be valid for the commit, or the run fails. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_Export . The main deploy is a full build: every index is rebuilt from the tree being published. See skill feature-staging, section Build types. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_Build . Build the L1 knowledge graph candidate, extracted See ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn. Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. 2295.title: Glossary: BPMN activities
2295.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 630 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 49 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 250 (SKOS) · smart-base 159 (SKOS) · who-iris 34 (SKOS). Split by first letter. 1167 terms are too many for one page within its budget of 1.0 MB, so they are on 3 pages by the first letter of the label. The ranges are fixed, so a term’s address does not move as terms are added. A label that does not start with a letter is on the first page. | A–D: 381 terms | E–Q: 364 terms | R–Z: 422 terms | .

2298.title: A
2298.content: ArchiMate model from the glossary candidate, extracted Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance's folio-glossary/v1 terms whose focus is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their skosConcept property (never by name) take the term's prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with --prune along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without --write it only reports; --check fails when anything would change. --seed goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under library/ (--from): an authored model is never a source of the glossary. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/archimate-from-glossary/archimate-from-glossary.ts#archimate-from-glossary . Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration candidate, extracted The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves the AST's resources (ast-data/ and <Type>-<id>.json), the artefact index and the sidecars, refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES, so the site build reports the IG's own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them. Per instance: index.json from the AST ig-cache.sh restore lays down from the IG repository's cache branch (authority: "cache"), menu.json from the IG's sushi-config.yaml at the commit cloned (recording the source.of and source.ref that stage-ig-sites clones from), releases.json from the repository's GitHub releases (a failed read writes nothing, never an empty list), package.tgz from the AST's resources, and the JSON-LD contexts the IG publishes. The first step of process ig-docs-site-compose. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/ig-index-build/ig-index-build.ts#ig-index-build . Build the review sheet's Apps Script and a document's Config tab candidate, extracted Builds Code.gs (--script), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from review-sheet.gs), and one document's Config tab rows (--config), filled from the folio's review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json, its review anchors and the draft's pdf-line-map.json. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet's links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each No. n linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document's URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet's Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs installTriggers; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With "mode": "drafting" in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document's table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab. 2300.title: C
2300.content: Catalogue a library from its bibliography candidate, extracted Write one folio-dublin-core/v1 record and one folio-catalogue-node/v1 item per library entry that the source ledger joins to a CSL-JSON reference, into the folio's declared catalogue directory, so gen-library-jsonld reads the title from the catalogue's dc.title instead of falling to the PDF or the slug. The join is exact: a ledger row naming the entry's structure.json source file, one reference id, and the same sha256 where both record one. Unjoined entries are reported and left alone. Never touches a node it did not write. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/catalogue-from-references/catalogue-from-references.ts#catalogue-from-references . Check a Questionnaire field for field against the wireframe it was derived from candidate, extracted Compare the data-element fields of a mid-fidelity wireframe (per data-layout, in document order) with the answerable items of a BUILT Questionnaire (depth first, named by definition or code). Reports a field with no item, an item with no field, an item naming no data element, a data element twice in one layout, and the first place the order differs. Fidelity, not design. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/check-wireframe-questionnaire/check-wireframe-questionnaire.ts#check-wireframe-questionnaire . Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes candidate, extracted The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. Tools of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/tools/review-log-watch/review-log-watch.ts#review-log-watch . Check an IG's built Questionnaires with CSIRO's SDC libraries candidate, extracted Build-time Structured Data Capture checks, one result per Questionnaire (sdcChecks[] of fhir-questionnaire-wireframe): assemble (@aehrc/sdc-assemble 2.0.3: an assemble-root's sub-forms resolve in this IG, and --out writes the assembled Questionnaire), template-extract (@aehrc/sdc-template-extract 1.0.16: extraction from the IG's fixture response yields the expected resources), populate (@aehrc/sdc-populate 4.7.2: FHIRPath pre-population from a fixture context gives the expected answers) and behaviour (@aehrc/questionnaire-test-toolkit 0.1.0: the IG's own behavioural test, warn-only). Checks only, no UI. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/sdc-checks/sdc-checks.ts#sdc-checks . Compile and check an IG's translation CodeSystem supplements candidate, extracted Compile the IG's CodeSystems with every input/fsh/translations/<locale>.fsh CodeSystem supplement in a throw-away FSHOnly SUSHI project, require 0 SUSHI errors, and check that each supplement's base CodeSystem is the IG's own, its codes are a subset of the base's, its language is the file's locale, and every CodeSystem id is unique. SUSHI is the version ig-toolchain.env pins, installed from scripts/sushi/package-lock.json with install scripts off; the FHIR core package is pinned by sha512; SUSHI runs with no network. Tools of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/tools/check-translation-supplements/check-translation-supplements.ts#check-translation-supplements . CSV tabular metadata candidate, extracted Read a delimited text file into a folio-tabular-csvw/v1 record: one table, its columns and their CSVW datatypes, each measured or explicitly undetermined. Routing is by content, never by extension: the first rows must agree on one field count of two or more, under exactly one of , ; TAB |. A CSV's fac:anchor sheet and cell are a determined null. Figure coverage and computability candidate, extracted For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). Dates are read through the number formats in styles.xml, not misread as integer serials. A malformed part is refused rather than half-read. Reads the ZIP with node:zlib and SpreadsheetML with fast-xml-parser. Governed by the tabular-metadata skill. 2315.title: Already somebody else’s concept?
2315.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4555 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4555 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

2511.doc: GDHCN Trust Network - Personal Health Wallet
2511.title: GDHCN Trust Network - Personal Health Wallet
2511.content: . This implementation guide is still being developed. Its content is for demonstration purposes only. Summary . This implementation guide specifies how a Personal Health Wallet (PHW) lets a person record privacy consent, share health information through verifiable health links, and have that consent enforced when the information is used. It uses IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR (PCF) 1.1.0 for consent directives and IHE Verifiable Health Links (VHL) 1.0.0-comment for the links. Every process is trust-anchor neutral: keys are published to, and trust lists read from, an abstract Trust Anchor. The WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN) is one possible Trust Anchor among others. The guide makes no claim of conformance to IHE Internet User Authorization (IUA). Supporting guidance, recommendations, resources and standards are listed in the Bibliography and on the Dependencies page. What this guide contains . | Consent: explicit and implied consent (IHE PCF), trust domains’ consent codes, and consent directives in shared and issued documents. | Business Processes: thirteen BPMN 2.0 processes: . | Consent and verifiable health links: A record and manage consent, B issue a consent-backed link, C present and redeem a link. | Data sharing agreements between servers: D register a client, E server-to-server access, F access decision, G audit and provenance, H revocation and suspension, I decide a link request under an agreement. | Shared certificate processes: J issue a certificate, K verify a certificate and its status. | Consent: L record explicit consent, M add consent directives to a shared or issued document. | . | Decision-support Logic: the DMN decision PHW.DT.AgreementAccess, which combines several agreements for one receiver. | Worked Example: IPS Pilgrimage (Hajj): processes A, B, C, F and I applied to one case. | System Actors, Sequence Diagrams and Transactions. | The logical models, profiles, value sets and examples are listed in the Artifact Index. An offline copy of the guide is on the Downloads page. | . How this guide is organised . This guide follows the levels of knowledge representation: . | Business Requirements: concepts, personas, business processes and decision logic. | Data Models and Exchange: actors, sequence diagrams, transactions and codings. | Deployment: security and privacy, testing, reference implementations and downloads. | . Disclaimer . This specification is a working draft for demonstration and may not be used for any implementation purposes. It is provided without warranty of completeness or consistency, and the official publication supersedes it. No liability can be inferred from the use or misuse of this specification or its consequences. 2515.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
2515.title: Lanes — who acts
2515.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Writes four records in a fixed order and touches the corpus graph in none of them — dublin-core as the record of truth, a manifest that references it, assets[] kept as a SIBLING of library: because that tree is regenerated and would drop anything written inside it, and finally the slug binding Task_Link depends on. A wrong order or placement is invisible until the next sync drops it. | .

2516.doc: Ingestion subprocess — build the L1 knowledge graph
2516.title: Steps
2516.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Write dublin-core.jsonld (the record of truth)Task_Dublin | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | One standalone Dublin Core record per folder. dcterms is already this corpus’s JSON-LD vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one. | . | Write manifest.jsonld referencing itTask_Manifest | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write manifest.jsonld for the folder: its @id, @type folio:SourceDocument, what it contains and its provenance, referencing the standalone dublin-core.jsonld as the record of truth rather than copying its fields. | . | Record assets[] — local path or remote URLTask_Assets | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | kind / role / url-or-path / checksum / retrieved. A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync. | . | Bind the folder to its bibliography slugTask_Bind | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Bind the folder name to the document’s bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them. | . | Read glossary and abbreviations into candidate termsTask_Glossary | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | glossary-terms | The source’s glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. Terms a person owns are never changed, and only a person moves a term to authored. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written. | . | Link L1 nodes into the corpus graphTask_Link | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact – paper, L2, L3 – resolves to it through library/. | .

2523.title: Ingestion subprocess — extract structure
2523.content: Process_ExtractStructure · advisory · 5 step(s) . Extract the structure of an uploaded source: its text layer, OCR where it has none, sections, structure and claim candidates. i i i i i

2524.title: How it connects
2524.content: . | Called by: L1 document ingestion — a document to the L1 source knowledge graph | Calls: none | Presented on: no docs page section shows this diagram | Running instances: none recorded | .

2525.title: Lanes — who acts
2525.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Two provenance paths converge on the same Task_Sections output — an embedded text layer extracted directly, or OCR that leaves the fuller text in ocr/ with only a stub in sections/ — and which branch this lane took is invisible downstream except to a grep that knows to check the fourth tier. Task_Candidates stays a proposal: nothing downstream may treat it as an adjudicated verdict. | .

2526.title: Steps
2526.content: Every one of the 5 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Extract the text layerTask_ExtractText | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. | . | OCR to ocr/page-*.txtTask_Ocr | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently (“Manual” and “Manval”), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. | . | Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matterTask_Sections | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief. | . | Write structure.jsonTask_Structure | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR’d text, source.runContext cites the OCR step’s run context by sha256. A title already known for the document (the catalogue’s dc.title, or one given with –title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections’ doc_title does not carry a scan’s misreading. | . | Extract claim candidatesTask_Candidates | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only – never adjudicated verdicts. | .

2527.title: Decisions
2527.content: Every one of the 1 decision(s) is documented. | decision | what decides it | branches | . | Embedded text layer?Gateway_HasText | Does the binary carry an embedded text layer? yes extracts it; no — scanned runs OCR into ocr/page-*.txt. | yes → Extract the text layerno — scanned → OCR to ocr/page-*.txt | .

2531.title: Lanes — who acts
2531.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | ingestion-agent | Runs both QA checks unattended and hands off exactly where the role’s persona says it must: Gateway_Drift’s ‘drift’ branch leaves this lane the moment a passage needs a judgement about which of two readings is right, rather than guessing; Task_Verdict, which records the outcome either way, stays in this lane, which owns the completeness verdict as a whole. | . | Reviewer (SME or editor) | reviewer | The only human involvement in this subprocess: a flagged passage where round-trip translation produced two different readings, and somebody has to say which is right. | .

2532.doc: Ingestion subprocess — the L1 completeness gate
2532.title: Steps
2532.content: Every one of the 4 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Is every derived artefact present?Task_CheckDerived | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | L1 source to L1 KG is NOT complete while a required derived artefact is missing. This is the gate that makes the derivation steps obligatory rather than aspirational. | . | Round-trip translation QATask_RoundTrip | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | translation-manageruntainted-verification | Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block’s <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO’s msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means “not yet run”, which is never a pass. | . | Adjudicate the flagged passageTask_FlagDrift | Reviewer (SME or editor) | calls Adjudicationdocument-intakeadjudication | A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. | . | Record the L1 completeness verdictTask_Verdict | Ingestion Engine (agent, runs unattended) | document-intake | Record the completeness verdict in three states — met, unmet, or not yet derivable — as bun run cat check:l1-complete reports it. 2571.doc: Are the .jsonld siblings still in sync with their .ts manifests?
2571.title: Are the .jsonld siblings still in sync with their .ts manifests?
2571.content: Process_JsonLdDrift · strict · 1 step(s) . Check that the committed .jsonld siblings are still in sync with the .ts manifests they are generated from. A GENERATED FILE THAT IS COMMITTED CAN GO STALE, AND A STALE ONE IS CONSULTED. Five --check runs in one job: the JSON-LD context, the block siblings, the library nodes, the site graph, and the label-resolution tests. Each regenerates from the .ts manifest that owns it and fails on any difference. They are drawn as ONE task rather than five, because they are independent of each other and sequential only because a single job runs them. Five boxes would assert an ordering the workflow does not have. The check itself is the shared generated-file-drift process (Process_GeneratedFileDrift), drawn once for every drift check. 2576.doc: A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories
2576.title: A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories
2576.content: Process_KgSeparation · strict · 19 step(s) . Move part of a knowledge graph into repositories of its own: the content (files to read, no code) and its tools (the code that writes and checks it) separate as a pair, into two repositories, not one. kg-separation.md is the practice; this is its order and its gates. Stages 1-3 are graph-detanglement, reused rather than restated. EVERY GATEWAY IS A COMMAND. Tools closed? is check:tools-closure with the content’s no-code test and a byte-identity check on the generated files; Every identifier its file's path? is check:node-iris; Green alone? is the standalone rehearsal; Ready to seed? is seed:ready --layer <name> --rehearse, decided by decisions/seed-readiness-gate.dmn. A check that could not run stops the process rather than reading as clean. A PERSON DECIDES FOUR TIMES, AND THE ADMINISTRATOR LANE SAYS WHERE: whether to separate at all, whether to authorise the extraction, creating the repositories, and the cutover. Nothing is committed to the new repositories before they are created, and the parent keeps its own copy until it consumes the first release. VERSIONS: the pair starts at the content’s version at the split, then each is versioned on its own; a tools release lists the content majors it supports. Examples: bootstrap and bootstrap-tools; cat-harness and cat-harness-tools. i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i i

2579.content: Every one of the 19 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Brief the workTask_Brief | Authoring agent | shared step GT_Briefopening-brief | What the work is and why, what is already measured with its provenance, how it will be done, and what would falsify the approach. The work item is already taken up when the process starts, so a sibling session sees the work before the brief is written.Here the work is a separation: what is separating, and why. | . | Measure the signalsTask_Measure | Authoring agent | kg-separation | Files and bytes per instance, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate’s cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package’s import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. | . | Separate this graph?Task_Decide | Administrator | calls Ask the personkg-separation | The owner decides from the measured signals, and also decides the address base for its identifiers, where verdicts about it live, and what its tools repository owns. Declining is a real outcome: the graph stays where it is. | . | 1–3 · Declare, detangle, isolateTask_Detangle | Authoring agent | graph-detanglement | The graph-detanglement practice, all of its gates: declared in place, zero wrong-direction edges on every axis, and standing alone with its own declaration, namespace and artefact. A plain task on purpose, not a call to graph-detanglement.bpmn: that process ends in its own authorise-and-extract steps, which here are stages 9-13 of this one, and calling it would run them twice. | . | 4 · Identity: version, iriBase, nodeSchemasTask_Identity | Platform authoring agent | kg-separation | The declaration carries name, version, iriBase, needs and nodeSchemas. A base move is bun run iri:sync -- --from <old base>, once; then iri:sync:check and check:node-iris are green. | . | 5 · Move harness output about it to the hostTask_Hosted | Platform authoring agent | kg-separation | QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test’s pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository’s, published to that repository’s qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. | . | 6 · Split content from toolsTask_Split | Platform authoring agent | kg-separation | Create <name>-tools as a sibling directory and move the code: the Zod source, the generators, the README and diagram writers, the content checks. Cut its import cone to its own files and declared packages. Both start at the content’s version. | . | 7 · Plan publicationTask_Plan | Publication manager | instance-publication | Every identifier the content mints is a file some step publishes: /v<major>/, for what programs read and pages people read alike; the exact release is the pin’s. Name collisions between published files are resolved here. | . | 8 · Rehearse standaloneTask_Rehearse | Build pipeline | kg-separation | Copy the content and the tools alone into a temporary directory, with nothing else on the path, and run the tools’ checks there. An empty tree must exit non-zero, so a rehearsal over nothing cannot pass. | . | Report what moves — sizes, what breaksTask_Propose | Authoring agent | shared step GT_ReportWhatMovesdeletion-requires-confirmation | The agent reports and waits: what would move, how large, what in the parent breaks, and the rollback. deletion-requires-confirmation is not a courtesy to waive: an agent never removes or relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. | . | 9 · Authorise the extractionTask_Authorise | Administrator | calls Ask the persondeletion-requires-confirmation | A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person’s decision. Declining leaves the graph declared, detangled, isolated and split in place. | . | Create the repositoriesTask_Create | Administrator | kg-separation | The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. | . | Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRsTask_Drain | Authoring agent | shared step GT_Drainkg-separation | Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer’s PRs, bring the layer’s open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. | . | 10 · Seed both repositoriesTask_Seed | Authoring agent | kg-separation | Seed main, then bring the content and the tools in as reviewed pull requests with their history, so neither repository’s first commit is unreviewable. The seed includes every publisher the declaration promises (sub-kg-lifecycle stage 10): a qa directory with storage needs .github/workflows/publish-qa.yml, the caller of the tools layer’s layer-qa-publish.yml, and test/results/ ignored. Without it the declared store is never written, and once the layer stops committing its results no reader finds them. | . | 11 · Parent consumes, additivelyTask_Consume | Platform authoring agent | calls Adopting an upstream version bumpupstream-version-adoption | The parent pins the pair (a commit while staging, a version once released) — a code dependency as a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json (remote-mount skill), never a submodule — repoints its imports, and keeps its own copy until it is green with the dependency declared. | . | 12 · First releaseTask_Release | Publication manager | package-release | Tag each repository, publish /v<major>/. From here the two are versioned independently; a tools release lists the content majors it supports. | . | Every identifier dereferencesTask_Verify | Build pipeline | calls Verify the export before it is deployedpublish-verification | After the release is live, every published identifier resolves to the file it names. | . | 13 · Cutover: retire the parent’s copyTask_Cutover | Administrator | deletion-requires-confirmation | The one commit worth reverting, made only after the parent consumes the release and every identifier dereferences. It retires the parent’s copy, frozen, never refreshed and never rendered, rather than deleting it. Where the copy goes is the sub-kg-lifecycle skill’s stage 13; this diagram does not name that store, because the published graph must not. | . | Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:checkTask_CutoverCheck | Build pipeline | kg-separation | Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream’s and is listed, not counted. | .

If the rehearsal could not run, that is not a pass: stop. | red: an unseen edge → 1–3 · Declare, detangle, isolatecould not run → UNKNOWN — stop. 2582.title: KG to public portal
2582.content: Process_KgToPortal · advisory · 10 step(s) . How a knowledge graph reaches a public portal this repository does not run: select, serialize, package, sign, distribute, and verify on the portal’s side. Three decisions belong to the DEPLOYMENT and are drawn as gateways rather than as steps — the ingestion transport, the versioned store, and the signing scheme. A pipeline that picks one of those is asserting a decision nobody made. A CDN is a LAYER, not a publication host. PUBLICATION_HOSTS answers “what serves the rendering”; a cache answers “what stands between the server and the reader”, and the canonical URL stays the origin’s either way. i i i i i i i i i i
